a507.speaker: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a507.name: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a507.speech: The organisation stated that the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and their allied militias also put the population at risk by surrounding with artillery the camps located on the outskirts of Goma, capital of North Kivu province.

a507.speaker: Clementine de Montjoye, HRW senior Africa researcher
a507.name: Clementine de Montjoye
a507.title: HRW senior Africa researcher
a507.speech: "As the conflict between Congolese and Rwandan forces and their allied militias approaches Goma, residents of the area and more than half a million displaced people are increasingly at risk of being caught up in the fighting and of being denied humanitarian aid," she said in a statement.

a507.speaker: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a507.name: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a507.speech: Since January 2024 HRW has documented five "illegal" attacks by the M23 and by Rwandan soldiers supporting the group on camps for internally displaced people or on densely populated areas near Goma, including the firing of at least three missiles at a camp on 3 May that killed 17 people, 15 of them children; according to HRW's investigation, Congolese troops and militias, as well as M23 rebels, regularly rape women in the camps or when they go out to collect firewood and food.

a507.speaker: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a507.name: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a507.speech: Denounced that this situation hampers the delivery of humanitarian aid to these camps and has led to food shortages for the population, since the organisations are caught in the crossfire between the parties.

a507.speaker: Clementine de Montjoye, HRW senior Africa researcher
a507.name: Clementine de Montjoye
a507.title: HRW senior Africa researcher
a507.speech: "Congo and Rwanda must recognise that abuses committed by one party to the conflict never justify abuses committed by the other; they must end their support for abusive armed groups and hold accountable those who commit war crimes," Montjoye said.

a507.speaker: Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a507.name: Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a507.speech: Revealed in early August that more than 10% of women aged 20 to 44 sheltering near Goma reported having been raped between November 2023 and April 2024.

a507.speaker: Rwandan authorities
a507.name: Rwandan authorities
a507.speech: Have always denied the alleged collaboration of Kigali with the M23.

a507.speaker: United Nations
a507.name: United Nations
a507.speech: Confirmed Rwanda's collaboration with the M23, and also confirmed the collaboration of the Congolese army with the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) rebels.

a507.speaker: Rwanda and the M23
a507.name: Rwanda and the M23
a507.speech: Accuse the Congolese army of collaborating with the rebels of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), founded in 2000 by leaders of the 1994 genocide and other (Hutu) Rwandans exiled in the DRCongo in order to recover political power in their country.

a537.speaker: Policy experts and researchers (published papers)
a537.name: Policy experts and researchers (published papers)
a537.speech: Have widely written in their published papers about Russia's alleged involvement in the political changes in these French colonies with the fractured economy and about the fact that the region constitutes a breeding field for armed Islamic jihadist groups, demonstrating Russia's first drastic step towards combating terrorism and ultimately penetrating into the entire G5 Sahel in West Africa.

a537.speaker: Moscow (Russian government, official statement)
a537.name: Moscow (Russian government
a537.title: official statement)
a537.speech: Officially said it was rather seriously concerned about the economic under-developments and the deepening instability as well as the impoverished population in the region.

a537.speaker: Vedomosti newspaper
a537.name: Vedomosti newspaper
a537.speech: Reported that Russian state-owned arms trader Rosoboronexport, as part of signed military-technical agreements, has delivered Russian-made combat and transport helicopters, armoured personnel carriers, small arms and ammunition to these Sahel-Saharan African countries.

a537.speaker: Oleg Ozerov, Ambassador-at-Large at the Russian Foreign Ministry and Head of the Secretariat of the Russia-Africa Partnership Forum
a537.name: Oleg Ozerov
a537.title: Ambassador-at-Large at the Russian Foreign Ministry and Head of the Secretariat of the Russia-Africa Partnership Forum
a537.speech: Spoke in an interview with RIA Novosti and explicitly pointed to the fact that Russia has no military bases nor military troops in Africa: "We don't have a military presence there. There are appeals to the Russian side for help in ensuring security. This is not a military presence. Military presence is when troops are sent. We send instructors at the request of the African states themselves. But all this is not a military presence."

a537.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a537.name: Vladimir Putin
a537.title: Russian President
a537.speech: In a Victory Day speech reminded, among other indelible facts, of the successful defeat of Nazism and asserted Russia's independence, and the support it (then the Soviet Union) provided others in their anti-colonial struggles and self-determination; stressed "Africa is now building up capacity and aspires to emerging as an effective powerhouse in a multipolar world with its unique identity by making confident strides in nurturing a genuine sense of political and economic sovereignty."

a537.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a537.name: Vladimir Putin
a537.title: Russian President
a537.speech: During exclusive talks with Guinea-Bissau's delegation, reiterated expanding bilateral partnership in economic, scientific and technological spheres, on grounds that ties between the two countries are rooted in long-standing traditions of friendship, as well as the principles of equality and mutual respect: "We have been maintaining effective inter-parliamentary and inter-agency ties too. Today, we have an opportunity to discuss our performance under bilateral agreements in various sectors and further steps to expand our cooperation. I must note that students from your country continue to study in Russia. We are ready to offer Guinea-Bissau an even bigger quota."

a537.speaker: Umaro Sissoco Embalo, Guinea-Bissau leader
a537.name: Umaro Sissoco Embalo
a537.title: Guinea-Bissau leader
a537.speech: On his part, expressed gratitude for the support which Russia has been giving to the Government and the people of Guinea-Bissau.

a537.speaker: Samir Bhattacharya, Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF)
a537.name: Samir Bhattacharya
a537.title: Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF)
a537.speech: Says Africa, especially the French-speaking West African countries, continue to face multiple democratic challenges with a wider negative impact across the region; that the narrative depicting Russia as a proactive coup advocate is compelling and seems to hold water; and that military takeovers have become a distinctive feature of regime change in West Africa ; said it would be overly generalizing to attribute the coups to neocolonialism alone, that a close examination reveals the Sahel Region has endured violent extremism, civil unrest and poor governance for a very long period, and that it unmistakably shows how France and other Western powers are losing ground in this region; frustration with France and other foreign powers increased fairly naturally as their military intervention failed to stem the Islamist insurgency; therefore the West cannot address the issue merely by blaming Russia, and Russia cannot blame only neocolonialism; Russia's engagement in Africa requires an in-depth study.

a537.speaker: Professor Sergiu Mișcoiu, Faculty of European Studies, Babes-Bolyai University (Cluj-Napoca, Romania), Director of the Centre for International Cooperation and Director of the Centre for African Studies
a537.name: Professor Sergiu Mișcoiu
a537.title: Faculty of European Studies, Babes-Bolyai University (Cluj-Napoca, Romania), Director of the Centre for International Cooperation and Director of the Centre for African Studies
a537.speech: Argued that neo-colonialism in Africa has been a growing reality after the end of the Cold War and reached a pinnacle by the early 2000s; that the more salient cases are the former French colonies and Russia is focused on uprooting France out of the continent; that Vladimir Putin has intended to restore the mightiness of the Soviet Union, including its influence over the African continent, but unlike the USSR, Russia didn't and doesn't dispose of the financial and logistic resources needed to massively invest in key sectors; that China, by comparison, has disposed of important financial resources and has been far less violent in spreading its influence, succeeding through investments in road and railway infrastructures, ports and major public buildings; and that Russia made almost no difference through its modest investments and bet its entire strategy on a mixture of the renewal of former USSR networks and the Soviet past, and direct intrusion in the domestic conflicts of the most vulnerable African states.

a651.speaker: Ousmane Diagana, Vice-President of the World Bank for West and Central Africa
a651.name: Ousmane Diagana
a651.title: Vice-President of the World Bank for West and Central Africa
a651.speech: has welcomed the escalation impact of the Northern Regions Social Cohesion Project (SOCO) on the lives of people, particularly those in poor rural communities in northern Ghana; said SOCO is a game changer and assured expedited action for the release of funds to continue the project and also increase the beneficiary communities ; “I am very satisfied. I have seen concrete activities that have been funded by the project. I am very impressed to see that there is a community at large that is a beneficiary of the project – that is the essence of the project. They consider it their project – so there is this sense of community-ownership which is critical” ; “I also understand that this is a need that was expressed by the community themselves. So, it means that we have been responsive to their needs. This is what this type of project is supposed to do. Of course, giving the magnitude of the need, it will be very important to put to good use what exists already – to have a very good communication about what the project activities are, so that the partners will be more encouraged to do more”.

a651.speaker: Ousmane Diagana, Vice-President of the World Bank for West and Central Africa
a651.name: Ousmane Diagana
a651.title: Vice-President of the World Bank for West and Central Africa
a651.speech: said the numerous requests for the extension of the project to non-beneficiary communities is a sign of the successes of the SOCO project, assuring that the World Bank will continue to support the project to achieve desired results; and was optimistic that governments in the four beneficiary countries, Ghana, Togo, Benin and Cote d’Ivoire, will also do their part to ensure the sustainability of the project.

a651.speaker: Robert Taliercio O’Brien, World Bank Ghana Country Director
a651.name: Robert Taliercio O’Brien
a651.title: World Bank Ghana Country Director
a651.speech: with some of the beneficiary MMDAs said feedback from them was very useful to the Bank to understand their need to see how the projects are structured to achieve desired results.

a651.speaker: Ministry of Local Government, Decentralisation and Rural Development (data)
a651.name: Ministry of Local Government
a651.title: Decentralisation and Rural Development (data)
a651.speech: According to data released by the Ministry, farmers who sell their cattle at the Livestock Market, which started operations on November 3, 2024, make income of about GHS400,000 each market day (Sunday), and income from the sale of small ruminants each market day is estimated at about GHS100,000.

a651.speaker: SOCO project implementers
a651.name: SOCO project implementers
a651.speech: said the investment made in these groups has brought about social cohesion by bringing the people together.

a651.speaker: Samuel Seth Passah, Director for Local Governance and Decentralisation
a651.name: Samuel Seth Passah
a651.title: Director for Local Governance and Decentralisation
a651.speech: speaking on behalf of the Chief Director at the engagement with project stakeholders, revealed the interest the SOCO project has attracted among Government and other development partners of the country and highlighted some of the progress made so far: “Within two years of the project’s effectiveness date, we have begun to see its impact on the ground across 48 districts, 217 clusters, covering 1,700 communities representing a population of 1.5 million. The project has also disbursed US$60 million (40%) out of the total US$150 million in the last two years”.

a651.speaker: Elizabeth Ohenewah Agyei, Coordinator of the SOCO project
a651.name: Elizabeth Ohenewah Agyei
a651.title: Coordinator of the SOCO project
a651.speech: said one challenging issue her outfit had had to battle with was how to get the minority groups in the community to participate in the project, but said continuous engagement with the minority groupings were yielding positive results, further solidifying the sustainability of the project ; noted that the project development goals have been achieved within two years of its implementation ; “Going forward, we should see how others who are looking forward to be beneficiaries are attended to. One of the things that we also look forward to is to be very specific to being able to measure the changes that are occurring. This is because if you are not able to measure the impact that these projects are making, then we won’t be able to know where exactly and how the next step will be”.

a653.speaker: Dr Aka Koffi Charles, Chief of Staff (Directeur de Cabinet) of the Ministry of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage of Côte d’Ivoire
a653.name: Dr Aka Koffi Charles
a653.title: Chief of Staff (Directeur de Cabinet) of the Ministry of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage of Côte d’Ivoire
a653.speech: revealed that this action will make it possible to catch up children aged 0 to 59 months who are not up to date or who have missed their vaccinations, and to supplement those who have not received vitamin A, and that this expansion of access to vaccination and vitamin A supplementation will certainly reduce poverty and establish universal health coverage ; declared: “Routine vaccination offers the opportunity for contact with the healthcare system from the very beginning of life and gives every child the chance to be in good health from the earliest age through to old age... the challenges we face are enormous and, for Côte d’Ivoire, it will be a matter of targeting zero-dose and under-vaccinated children from 2020 to 2023 linked to the coronavirus pandemic.” ; invited all parents to have their children benefit from the big catch-up, bringing them to health centres and to vaccination and vitamin A supplementation posts in order to protect them against the increased risks of epidemics of diseases such as measles, polio and diphtheria.

a749.speaker: Zabihullah Mujahid, Taliban administration spokesperson
a749.name: Zabihullah Mujahid
a749.title: Taliban administration spokesperson
a749.speech: Confirmed that at least 1,411 people have died, 3,124 have been injured, and more than 5,400 houses have been destroyed.

a749.speaker: Afghan Red Crescent Society
a749.name: Afghan Red Crescent Society
a749.speech: According to the humanitarian group working in the region, more people are feared trapped under rubble.

a749.speaker: U.N. coordinator in Afghanistan
a749.name: U.N. coordinator in Afghanistan
a749.speech: Warned that the toll was likely to rise further.

a749.speaker: Afghan authorities
a749.name: Afghan authorities
a749.speech: Said on Tuesday that the death toll from Afghanistan's worst earthquake in years had risen to more than 1,400, with thousands more injured.

a749.speaker: Reuters (report)
a749.name: Reuters (report)
a749.speech: Had reported as of Monday that the death toll had already surpassed 800, with at least 2,800 people injured.

a749.speaker: Taliban spokesperson (quoted by SaharaReporters, October 2023)
a749.name: Taliban spokesperson (quoted by SaharaReporters
a749.title: October 2023)
a749.speech: Said that powerful earthquakes in western Afghanistan killed at least 2,000 people, describing those quakes as "some of the deadliest ones to strike the country in two decades."

a749.speaker: Spokesperson for Afghanistan's National Disaster Management Authority (reported by AP)
a749.name: Spokesperson for Afghanistan's National Disaster Management Authority (reported by AP)
a749.speech: Said a magnitude-6.3 earthquake in that incident was followed by strong aftershocks on Saturday.

a749.speaker: United States Geological Survey
a749.name: United States Geological Survey
a749.speech: According to the USGS, the epicentre was about 40 km (25 miles) northwest of Herat City, followed by three major aftershocks measuring magnitude 6.3, 5.9, and 5.5, along with several weaker shocks.

a783.speaker: Charge sheet (court record)
a783.name: Charge sheet (court record)
a783.speech: According to the charge sheet, Khetas Sibanda, 16, Kelvin Maposa, 43, Matshidza Sibanda, 33, and Kholwani Sibanda, 39, are charged with illegal mining of minerals; the particulars of the offence are that, on or about July 26 at or near Rainbow Mine in Matsiloje, acting together with a common purpose, they were unlawfully found with mineral deposits.

a850.speaker: Ivete Alane, Mozambican Minister of Labour, Gender and Social Action
a850.name: Ivete Alane
a850.title: Mozambican Minister of Labour, Gender and Social Action
a850.speech: Announced this Thursday that it is estimated that more than 2,000 workers will become unemployed in the country: "From the last meeting I had with the group of organisations that benefited from the funding, they spoke of 2,500 posts and I believe it must be more or less that."

a850.speaker: Ivete Alane, Mozambican Minister of Labour, Gender and Social Action
a850.name: Ivete Alane
a850.title: Mozambican Minister of Labour, Gender and Social Action
a850.speech: Considers that the way out lies in the flourishing of the national economy: "Considering that jobs are being lost, and that is a problem, our expectation is that the economy will flourish so that jobs can be created in Mozambique."

a850.speaker: US Ambassador to Mozambique
a850.name: US Ambassador to Mozambique
a850.speech: Warned in February of this year, through a cable, that the absence of USAID staff in the country would leave 114 ongoing funding initiatives and 225 junior workers in uncertainty.

a850.speaker: Humanitarian aid specialists and international organisations
a850.name: Humanitarian aid specialists and international organisations
a850.speech: Strongly criticised the end of USAID, warning that its disappearance leaves an enormous gap in health, education and humanitarian crisis response programmes.

a850.speaker: Barack Obama and George W. Bush, former US presidents
a850.name: Barack Obama and George W. Bush
a850.title: former US presidents
a850.speech: Directed criticism at the Trump government on Monday at a farewell event for USAID.

a850.speaker: Study coordinated by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal), published in The Lancet
a850.name: Study coordinated by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal)
a850.title: published in The Lancet
a850.speech: Warned that cuts to North American aid could lead to more than 14 million "avoidable" deaths by 2030; according to the study, USAID had a fundamental impact in reducing mortality from HIV/AIDS, malaria and neglected tropical diseases across the world.

a1020.speaker: Statistics (cited)
a1020.name: Statistics (cited)
a1020.speech: Statistics indicate that every year between fifty and one hundred thousand women develop new obstetric fistulas.

a1020.speaker: Health analysts
a1020.name: Health analysts
a1020.speech: Say obstetric fistula is associated with devastating lifelong morbidity with severe medical, social, psychological and economic consequences.

a1020.speaker: ECOWAS, through the ECOWAS Gender Development Centre (EGDC)
a1020.name: ECOWAS
a1020.title: through the ECOWAS Gender Development Centre (EGDC)
a1020.speech: Listed the fight against obstetric fistula as a priority area of intervention in connection with SDG 3 and SDG 5, which relate respectively to women's health and gender equality.

a1050.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a1050.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a1050.title: Israeli Prime Minister
a1050.speech: Declared before boarding the plane that on Tuesday the two leaders would discuss "the victory against Hamas, the return of all our hostages and the fight against the Iranian axis in all its dimensions."

a1050.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1050.name: Donald Trump
a1050.title: US President
a1050.speech: During his first term repeatedly said that Israel had "never had a better friend in the White House."

a1050.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1050.name: Donald Trump
a1050.title: US President
a1050.speech: Proposed to "simply clean out" Gaza and to transfer the Palestinians to "safer" places such as Egypt or Jordan, provoking an international outcry.

a1050.speaker: Celine Touboul, co-director of the Economic Cooperation Foundation (ECF), Tel Aviv
a1050.name: Celine Touboul
a1050.title: co-director of the Economic Cooperation Foundation (ECF), Tel Aviv
a1050.speech: "For Netanyahu, a privileged relationship with the White House is an essential tool."

a1081.speaker: Adelheid Marschang, WHO emergency director
a1081.name: Adelheid Marschang
a1081.title: WHO emergency director
a1081.speech: "Access to humanitarian aid continues to be severely limited by the military presence around health and treatment centres," she declared today to the United Nations in Geneva, Switzerland. She stressed, however, that bureaucratic obstacles and military roadblocks are disrupting the distribution of aid "where it is most needed."

a1081.speaker: Adelheid Marschang, WHO emergency director
a1081.name: Adelheid Marschang
a1081.title: WHO emergency director
a1081.speech: Warned that the situation is "particularly alarming" in the eastern regions of the country, such as North Kivu, where more than 12,800 cholera cases and 21 deaths related to the disease were recorded up to 30 June.

a1081.speaker: Adelheid Marschang, WHO emergency director
a1081.name: Adelheid Marschang
a1081.title: WHO emergency director
a1081.speech: Lamented that the crisis in the DR Congo "continues to be one of the most underfunded," with only 26% of the funds requested to date raised to help an estimated 25.4 million people affected by the conflict. She therefore appealed for "sustained and unimpeded" access and asked the international community to work together to restore peace and improve the mental and physical health of the whole population of the DR Congo.

a1081.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report
a1081.name: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report
a1081.speech: Reported that about 40% of the population (40.8 million people) suffer from severe food shortages, with armed conflict and displacement the main causes of growing food insecurity in the country.

a1247.speaker: Senator Adamu Aliero
a1247.name: Senator Adamu Aliero
a1247.speech: Observes that “Virtually all the revenue generating agencies have met their targets – the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, the Federal Inland Revenue Service and Nigeria Customs Service… Some have even exceeded it by more than 20 per cent. The issue is, ‘Why do we go borrowing if we have actually met our target?’ What are we doing with (the) excess revenue?” ; wonders why Nigeria still takes loans, despite claims by the Tinubu administration that the nation is earning more.

a1247.speaker: Richard Wolff, American Marxian economist
a1247.name: Richard Wolff
a1247.title: American Marxian economist
a1247.speech: Has a deeply contrary opinion about loans that America is taking from its intense competitor, China, which greedily snaps up its Treasury Bills and Treasury Bonds; argues that Americans must find a way to cough out considerable tax in order to service and pay back the $800 billion that Uncle Sam, the world biggest debtor, owes China.

a1247.speaker: Fact-check (unnamed)
a1247.name: Fact-check (unnamed)
a1247.speech: Has proven to be a hoax the claim that Mali has paid up all its debts; it paid only a part of it.

a1247.speaker: Some reports (unnamed)
a1247.name: Some reports (unnamed)
a1247.speech: Claim that Nigeria’s tax receipts increased by 56 per cent in 2023.

a1369.speaker: Officials of the White House
a1369.name: Officials of the White House
a1369.speech: "disclosed this on Monday, according to the BBC" - that Mr Trump reportedly plans to merge USAID with the State Department to boost its efficiency and ensure its funds align with his administration's agenda.

a1369.speaker: BBC
a1369.name: BBC
a1369.speech: Cited as the source for the report that White House officials disclosed the merger plan on Monday.

a1369.speaker: USAID agency leadership (email to employees)
a1369.name: USAID agency leadership (email to employees)
a1369.speech: Employees still in the system "received emails saying 'at the direction of agency leadership', the headquarters building 'will be closed to agency personnel on Feb. 3.'"

a1369.speaker: Elon Musk, appointed by President Trump to oversee the potential merger
a1369.name: Elon Musk
a1369.title: appointed by President Trump to oversee the potential merger
a1369.speech: "heavily criticised USAID, calling it a 'criminal organisation.'"

a1369.speaker: Chris Van Hollen, US Senator from Maryland
a1369.name: Chris Van Hollen
a1369.title: US Senator from Maryland
a1369.speech: "We would like to see firsthand what is happening to this essential agency that does such good work for the American people" ; "We will do everything we can to block State Department nominees from going forward until this illegal action is reversed" ; noted that they would have to rely on courts without the support of Republicans.

a1369.speaker: Democrats (several congressmen and women protesting at the USAID building)
a1369.name: Democrats (several congressmen and women protesting at the USAID building)
a1369.speech: After being denied entry into the office, "the democrats promised to block state department nominees for as long as USAID remains threatened."

a1369.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a1369.name: Marco Rubio
a1369.title: US Secretary of State
a1369.speech: Said he has been appointed as acting administrator of the agency; in a letter to lawmakers, announced that he had appointed Pete Marocco as the acting administrator and said he had authorised Mr Marocco "to begin the process of engaging in a review and potential reorganisation of USAID's activities to maximise efficiency and align operations with the national interest" ; "The Department of State and other pertinent entities will be consulting with Congress and the appropriate committees to reorganise and absorb certain bureaus, offices, and missions of USAID."

a1369.speaker: Aid groups and officials
a1369.name: Aid groups and officials
a1369.speech: Have accused Pete Marocco of deliberately undermining the agency.

a1496.speaker: NRA Election Manifesto 2025-2030 (party document)
a1496.name: NRA Election Manifesto 2025-2030 (party document)
a1496.speech: At the heart of the NRA's Election Manifesto 2025-2030 is the conviction that effective utilisation of Tanzania's abundant natural resources can generate enough revenue to finance free education, healthcare and water services. The manifesto stresses cutting unnecessary expenditure, strengthening governance and ensuring that the wealth of the nation benefits all citizens equally. ; The NRA manifesto pledges to eliminate poverty, maintain peace, uphold accountability, strengthen the Union and instill patriotism across all sectors of society.

a1496.speaker: Hassan Almas, National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.name: Hassan Almas
a1496.title: National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.speech: argued that Tanzania's future lies not in foreign aid or endless borrowing, but in smart management of its natural endowments from minerals and gas to vast water bodies and fertile land. "Our goal is to make Tanzania self-reliant by harnessing what we already have," he said. "We must stop wasteful spending and channel our resources into essential services that directly improve people's lives."

a1496.speaker: Hassan Almas, National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.name: Hassan Almas
a1496.title: National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.speech: Proposed a sweeping plan to halve government expenditure by reducing the number of ministries to just ten, each consisting of specialised departments led by technocrats rather than politicians, saying this model will enhance professionalism, cut bureaucracy and save billions that can be redirected to priority sectors like education and health. "Many ministries today are politically driven rather than performance-based. Politicians often think about re-election rather than service delivery," he remarked. "We will create a lean, efficient government that works for citizens, not for politics." ; He explained the restructuring is designed to promote accountability and eliminate overlapping functions that drain public funds.

a1496.speaker: Hassan Almas, National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.name: Hassan Almas
a1496.title: National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.speech: Added that his administration would introduce a single tax collection system, replacing multiple agencies such as the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) and district councils that often create loopholes for evasion. "This unified system will simplify revenue collection, reduce corruption and ensure steady funding for national development programmes," he said.

a1496.speaker: Hassan Almas, National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.name: Hassan Almas
a1496.title: National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.speech: Argued that election manifestos are too transient and tied to party interests, and that a National Development Policy (NDP) would serve as a non-partisan document guaranteeing policy stability and continuity in major infrastructure, education and industrialisation projects. "Under the NRA, manifestos will become inputs, not the master plan," he said. "The National Development Policy will remain the guiding document for all future governments, regardless of which party is in power." ; Said such a framework would protect Tanzania from frequent policy reversals and ensure that each administration builds on the achievements of its predecessor instead of starting afresh.

a1496.speaker: Hassan Almas, National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.name: Hassan Almas
a1496.title: National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.speech: Pledged to approve dual citizenship to enable Tanzanians living abroad to participate fully in the country's economic transformation, saying the diaspora community — rich in skills, capital and global exposure — could play a vital role in modernising Tanzania's technological landscape, especially through investment in ICT and knowledge transfer. "This will strengthen our human capital and integrate Tanzania into the global digital economy," he said.

a1496.speaker: Hassan Almas, National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.name: Hassan Almas
a1496.title: National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.speech: Promised to push for the completion of the new constitution from where the 2014 Draft left off, said his government will prioritise laws that reflect the will of all Tanzanians, and promised to pardon political prisoners as a gesture of national healing, pledging a new era that embraces the rule of law, freedom of expression, press freedom and political tolerance. "We must begin a new chapter of reconciliation. Tanzania's progress depends on peace, respect for differences and the freedom to express divergent opinions," Almas noted.

a1496.speaker: Hassan Almas, National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.name: Hassan Almas
a1496.title: National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.speech: Said the NRA will enforce strict laws against same-sex relations, arguing that moral decay undermines the nation's social fabric, and that African leaders have often limited themselves to speeches and condemnations without taking legislative action, allowing harmful practices to persist. "Society must be guided by values that protect future generations," he said, framing the issue as one of cultural preservation rather than discrimination.

a1496.speaker: Hassan Almas, National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.name: Hassan Almas
a1496.title: National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.speech: Said his government would build on the achievements of the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) while injecting new energy into ongoing projects, citing the Standard Gauge Railway (SGR), road network expansion and energy infrastructure as transformative undertakings that deserve continuity but with faster and more accountable execution. "The ruling party has done a lot, but it has grown tired. While the world is running, they are walking," he quipped. "We want to make them run again so Tanzania can rise from a lower-middleincome economy to a highincome one."

a1496.speaker: Hassan Almas, National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.name: Hassan Almas
a1496.title: National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.speech: Envisioned a coalition government that recruits leaders from across the political divide, regardless of party affiliation. "Why should we exclude capable Tanzanians because of party membership? Under NRA, recruitment will be based on merit, patriotism and competence, not political loyalty," he said.

a1496.speaker: Hassan Almas, National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.name: Hassan Almas
a1496.title: National Reconstruction Alliance (NRA) presidential candidate
a1496.speech: Urged ordinary Tanzanians — farmers, workers, students and entrepreneurs — to view the 2025 election as a turning point. "Our mission is to rebuild this nation from a mindset shaped by division to one rooted in unity and patriotism," he told supporters during a rally in Kigoma, his home region. "We want a Tanzania where every citizen feels ownership of the country's progress."

a1590.speaker: South African National Defence Force (SANDF)
a1590.name: South African National Defence Force (SANDF)
a1590.speech: The scheduled arrival of the Tupolev Tu-160 jets at Air Force Base Waterkloof on Oct. 29 "has been postponed," the South African National Defence Force said in a brief statement Wednesday ; the trip had been meant to "reaffirm the diplomatic ties" between the countries, the military said in a separate statement on Tuesday.

a1590.speaker: Tass, Russian news agency
a1590.name: Tass
a1590.title: Russian news agency
a1590.speech: reported on Monday that the two nations' armies agreed to deepen their cooperation.

a1590.speaker: Russian Embassy in South Africa (@EmbassyofRussia), social media post
a1590.name: Russian Embassy in South Africa (@EmbassyofRussia)
a1590.title: social media post
a1590.speech: "Russia's youngest White Swan - another photo of a recently completed #Tupolev Tu-160 - first one built in 10 years - taking it to the skies during its maiden test flight"

a1590.speaker: Piotr Matys, currency analyst at InTouch Capital Markets
a1590.name: Piotr Matys
a1590.title: currency analyst at InTouch Capital Markets
a1590.speech: "Some Western investors may become concerned that South Africa intends to further enhance cooperation with Russia's armed forces" ; "Western countries led by the US could potentially penalise South Africa over its relationship with Russia, which would have negative consequences for the rand."

a1590.speaker: Democratic Alliance (DA), statement
a1590.name: Democratic Alliance (DA)
a1590.title: statement
a1590.speech: said in a statement that the plan to receive two of Russia's so-called Blackjack bombers raised questions over South Africa's non-aligned stance in global conflicts ; "If South Africa's neutrality is genuine, the DA calls on Ramaphosa to extend the same invitation to Ukraine's military personnel and equipment that has been extended to Russia."

a1590.speaker: Reuben Brigety, US ambassador to South Africa
a1590.name: Reuben Brigety
a1590.title: US ambassador to South Africa
a1590.speech: triggered a diplomatic furor last year when he alleged that Pretoria supplied weapons to Russia.

a1590.speaker: A judicial inquiry (South Africa)
a1590.name: A judicial inquiry (South Africa)
a1590.speech: found no evidence to back the allegations that Pretoria supplied weapons to Russia.

a1590.speaker: Ambassador Reuben Brigety (@USAmbRSA), social media post
a1590.name: Ambassador Reuben Brigety (@USAmbRSA)
a1590.title: social media post
a1590.speech: "Advancing our strategic defense partnership, including USA-RSA Exercise Shared Accord 2025, topped the agenda of my meeting w/Min of Defence & Military Veterans, Angie Motshekga. We can accomplish a great deal together."

a1653.speaker: Filippo Grandi, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a1653.name: Filippo Grandi
a1653.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a1653.speech: Warned on Thursday that millions of lives are at risk following the "brutal cuts" in the funding of international aid operations ; "The consequences for people fleeing danger will be immediate and devastating," he warned in the statement, explaining that "with less funding, fewer staff and a reduced UNHCR presence in countries hosting refugees, the equation is simple: lives will be lost."

a1653.speaker: Filippo Grandi, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a1653.name: Filippo Grandi
a1653.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a1653.speech: Also sent an internal communication to his staff informing them of the situation and announcing that the organisation will be forced to cut jobs ; "We call on member states to honour their commitments to displaced people. The time has come, not for retreat, but for solidarity."

a1653.speaker: Notícias ao Minuto (news outlet, cited as source)
a1653.name: Notícias ao Minuto (news outlet
a1653.title: cited as source)
a1653.speech: According to Notícias ao Minuto, Grandi also sent an internal communication to his staff informing them of the situation and announcing that the organisation will be forced to cut jobs.

a1698.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1698.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1698.title: President of Ghana
a1698.speech: Called for a fundamental shift in Ghana's economic approach, urging the nation to move beyond reliance on foreign aid and IMF bailouts and focus on self-sufficiency and domestic resource mobilisation; stressed that Ghana's continued dependence on imports, donor aid, and financial assistance from external agencies undermines the true essence of independence: "Discussions about our independence often highlight our reliance on imports, on donor aid, and IMF bailouts as signs of continued dependence" ; "This reminder is repeated so often that while undeniably real, it risks becoming a cliché. Yet the entire efficacy of this reminder lies not in just repeating it, but in our willingness to take decisive action."

a1698.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1698.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1698.title: President of Ghana
a1698.speech: Criticised what he described as empty rhetoric on self-reliance, warning that Ghana cannot claim to be an Africa beyond aid while still returning to donors for financial assistance: "Proclaiming self-reliance while marching straight back to the donors into the hands of the donor agencies, begging bowl in hand, is really meaningless," he declared.

a1698.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1698.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1698.title: President of Ghana
a1698.speech: Outlined a series of policies his administration is implementing to achieve true economic independence, including fiscal discipline, economic expansion, and enhanced domestic revenue generation, revealing the 24-hour economy programme designed to ensure continuous economic activity, job expansion, and increased productivity: "This administration is working to implement the 24-hour economy programme to ensure that our economy never goes to sleep," he said; according to the President, this policy will boost exports, reduce dependence on foreign imports, and enhance Ghana's trade footprint.

a1698.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1698.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1698.title: President of Ghana
a1698.speech: Highlighted the $10 billion Big Push Initiative, which aims to modernise infrastructure, create jobs, and stimulate local industries; stressed the need to prioritise agriculture as a key driver of economic transformation, citing the country's over $2 billion annual expenditure on food imports as a major setback to self-sufficiency: "Agriculture remains our biggest opportunity to reduce import dependence," he said; explained that the Feed Ghana programme will drive mass food production, while the Poultry Farm to Table Initiative will boost domestic poultry production to reduce Ghana's 95% reliance on imported poultry products.

a1698.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1698.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1698.title: President of Ghana
a1698.speech: Called on young Ghanaians to embrace the opportunities presented by these policies and contribute to nation-building: "Policies alone, no matter how well crafted and well-intentioned, will not change our reality. Action will change that reality," he emphasised ; "Young Ghanaians must step up to the plate, seize these opportunities, and contribute to building a self-sufficient nation."

a1800.speaker: Reverend Brian Kamwendo, presidential adviser on religious affairs (Malawi)
a1800.name: Reverend Brian Kamwendo
a1800.title: presidential adviser on religious affairs (Malawi)
a1800.speech: Stated during a national service of worship on July 5, as part of the 61st independence anniversary celebrations in Lilongwe, that about 5 300 clerics have accessed K8.3 billion loans from the National Economic Empowerment Fund (Neef).

a1800.speaker: Malawi Conference of Catholic Bishops (MCCB), Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and Muslim Association of Malawi (MAM)
a1800.name: Malawi Conference of Catholic Bishops (MCCB)
a1800.title: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and Muslim Association of Malawi (MAM)
a1800.speech: Said yesterday that none of their members has reported getting the said loans, and that they were not approached by authorities on the same.

a1800.speaker: Valeriano Mtseka, MCCB general secretary
a1800.name: Valeriano Mtseka
a1800.title: MCCB general secretary
a1800.speech: Said in an interview yesterday that he was not aware of any cleric affiliated to his religious body having benefitted from the arrangement. "I don't know of any [Catholic] priest or bishop who has benefitted from this loan," he said in a WhatsApp text response.

a1800.speaker: Reverend Billy Gama, MCC board chairperson
a1800.name: Reverend Billy Gama
a1800.title: MCC board chairperson
a1800.speech: Expressed surprise with Kamwendo's statement that 5 300 clerics have so far benefitted from Neef loans, and said that as MCC chairperson, his office was procedurally supposed to be informed about the purported Neef loans to the clergy. Said Gama: "Actually, I was right there at the prayers and I was shocked when I heard that statement because to the best of my knowledge, no one [affiliated to MCC] has benefitted from the said loans. I was even tempted to ask Brian 'who are the people who have benefited?' It can be a political statement. But I just let it go."

a1800.speaker: Sheikh Dinala Chabulika, MAM publicity secretary
a1800.name: Sheikh Dinala Chabulika
a1800.title: MAM publicity secretary
a1800.speech: Said that following Kamwendo's statement, the association moved to establish whether some of its members were among the beneficiaries. "We have found zero. Write [the story] and tell them [government] that we [MAM] haven't found anyone [who has received Neef loan]," he said.

a1800.speaker: Reverend Brian Kamwendo, presidential adviser on religious affairs (Malawi)
a1800.name: Reverend Brian Kamwendo
a1800.title: presidential adviser on religious affairs (Malawi)
a1800.speech: Said in an interview last evening that he was not surprised that some major religious bodies were not aware that some of their clerics have benefitted from K8.3 billion Neef loans; he said the loan beneficiaries were "fraternal clerics", as such it was justifiable that the clerics' mother bodies have no details. "We started with the fraternal because this was just a pilot phase with an expectation that we will later engage the mother bodies. So, it is not strange that they don't know who have benefitted."

a1800.speaker: Whyghtone Mweta, Neef credit manager
a1800.name: Whyghtone Mweta
a1800.title: Neef credit manager
a1800.speech: Said in a separate interview that the 5 300 clerics were drawn from the country's religious denominations after they formed groups and accessed the loans under the Faith Leaders Empowerment Scheme. "They [clerics] are into the whole spectrum of businesses, some are running grocery shops; some are into farming, while others are Airtel Money agents. So we treat them as any eligible Malawian who can benefit from Neef loans," he said.

a1800.speaker: National Economic Empowerment Fund (Neef)
a1800.name: National Economic Empowerment Fund (Neef)
a1800.speech: On June 26 2025 dismissed reports that it had disbursed about K5.8 billion to 11 pastors under a purported Presidential Initiative on Sustainable Community Empowerment; earlier this year Neef said it targeted to disburse K150 billion to 400 000 farmers and entrepreneurs by March this year.

a1873.speaker: Dr. Alemayehu Kiri, medical director of Guduru Primary Hospital
a1873.name: Dr. Alemayehu Kiri
a1873.title: medical director of Guduru Primary Hospital
a1873.speech: "We have a shortage of emergency drugs. No operating room sets. We do not have beds. And now there is also a shortage of water supply due to the damage to the water reservoir. The community pharmacy was also destroyed, and all the drugs and materials were taken."

a1873.speaker: Mulu Takele, displaced mother of seven
a1873.name: Mulu Takele
a1873.title: displaced mother of seven
a1873.speech: explained: "The gunshots were unbearable, so we fled to save our lives. It was a nightmare and very difficult for my children. We lost everything and have not received any assistance since we arrived in Balo. No one has come to ask about our situation."

a1873.speaker: Julian Jaccard, ICRC head of sub-delegation in Nekemte
a1873.name: Julian Jaccard
a1873.title: ICRC head of sub-delegation in Nekemte
a1873.speech: said: "We have had to make difficult choices, targeting places with little presence of other humanitarian actors." ; "People in these areas have suffered immensely and for a long time."

a1873.speaker: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) (figures released)
a1873.name: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) (figures released)
a1873.speech: Since January 2023, in Oromia, the ICRC has assisted 62,800 people with food, household supplies, shelter and cash; regularly supported 12 health facilities with medical supplies and equipment; helped 32,500 people restore or maintain family links; and facilitated access to clean water for 187,000 people.

a1973.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (press release)
a1973.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (press release)
a1973.speech: Announced that it today launched its Islamic Philanthropy Fund, a new initiative that aims to harness the power of Islamic charitable giving to support some of the world's most vulnerable people; said the Fund is an important milestone for IOM as global crises worsen and human displacement increases, and that in its inaugural year the Fund is prioritizing the Sudan Emergency Response by delivering cash to displaced families, those stranded at borders, and communities in urgent need of humanitarian assistance.

a1973.speaker: Amy Pope, IOM Director General
a1973.name: Amy Pope
a1973.title: IOM Director General
a1973.speech: “With today’s complex crises displacing record numbers of people and causing immeasurable suffering, it’s critical to harness the spirit of Islamic charity to help alleviate suffering, empower communities to rebuild and thrive, and protect the dignity of people in need” ; “We are both honored and excited to announce IOM’s Islamic Philanthropy Fund as a means to help us engage Muslims around the world and channel their contributions through a trusted and efficient platform, maximising their positive impact.”

a2096.speaker: International Monetary Fund (Global Financial Stability Report, October 2024)
a2096.name: International Monetary Fund (Global Financial Stability Report
a2096.title: October 2024)
a2096.speech: Highlights the growing vulnerabilities of the global financial system; the indicators for sub-Saharan Africa reveal specific challenges, while calling for concerted action to prevent a systemic crisis. The report warns of long-term risks and the need to strengthen financial systems.

a2096.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2096.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2096.speech: Has observed a deterioration in global economic activity since its last report in April 2024, despite the monetary easing efforts led by the main central banks. According to the IMF's "growth-at-risk" indicator, short-term global financial stability risks remain contained within the most favourable 40% of recent history; however, the Fund warns that this apparent stability masks structural fragilities which, if ignored, could translate into major crises.

a2096.speaker: International Monetary Fund (Global Financial Stability Report, October 2024)
a2096.name: International Monetary Fund (Global Financial Stability Report
a2096.title: October 2024)
a2096.speech: According to the report, the global banking sector could see its profitability compromised by falling interest rates, thus limiting the possibilities of support in the event of a crisis in emerging economies.

a2096.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2096.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2096.speech: Recalls that the uncertainty accumulated by ongoing conflicts and the strategic choices of certain leaders could cause uncertainty, asset revaluations and surges in risk preference, as in August 2024, when the stock markets of Japan and the United States recorded sudden falls.

a2096.speaker: International Monetary Fund (Global Financial Stability Report, October 2024)
a2096.name: International Monetary Fund (Global Financial Stability Report
a2096.title: October 2024)
a2096.speech: Raises the rise of artificial intelligence in trading and investment activities as another point of attention: while it can generate savings and efficiency gains, AI is also a potential source of opacity and of risks that accumulate in times of tension.

a2096.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2096.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2096.speech: Urges policymakers to adopt macroprudential and budgetary measures to prevent a major financial crisis. In countries where inflation dynamics persist, the Fund suggests clear communication and a gradual adjustment of monetary policy. For sub-Saharan African nations where public debt has exploded following the successive crises of the last decade, priority must be given to rebuilding fiscal buffers, supported by credible tax policy reforms. The IMF also recommends strengthening the regulation of non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs), which play a growing role in capital markets, particularly in Africa where they facilitate access to private credit.

a2103.speaker: Vitumbiko Mumba, Malawi Congress Party presidential running mate and Minister of Trade and Industry
a2103.name: Vitumbiko Mumba
a2103.title: Malawi Congress Party presidential running mate and Minister of Trade and Industry
a2103.speech: Says President Lazarus Chakwera's re-election bid is anchored on a practical and integrated development plan focused on food security, wealth creation and responsive public service delivery; outlined five core pillars that he said summarise the MCP manifesto, which he described as the most coordinated and achievable in the country's democratic history; stressed the need to build strong national reserves to cushion citizens from recurring disasters and reduce dependency on external humanitarian assistance: "We should be able to keep our own resources for the sake of disasters. When floods or droughts strike, Malawians must not suffer or wait for handouts. We should be ready to respond using what we have."

a2103.speaker: Vitumbiko Mumba, Malawi Congress Party presidential running mate and Minister of Trade and Industry
a2103.name: Vitumbiko Mumba
a2103.title: Malawi Congress Party presidential running mate and Minister of Trade and Industry
a2103.speech: Justifying the feasibility of the MCP's plans, cited his own K500 million Mumba Revolving Fund initiative in his Mzimba Central Constituency as evidence that well-structured development programmes can work.

a2103.speaker: Richard Chimwendo Banda, MCP secretary general and Minister of Local Government, Unity and Culture
a2103.name: Richard Chimwendo Banda
a2103.title: MCP secretary general and Minister of Local Government, Unity and Culture
a2103.speech: Took a jibe at rivals Democratic Progressive Party's (DPP) presidential candidate Peter Mutharika whom he described as too old to even attend his own manifesto launch; he also disclosed plans to elevate more traditional leaders ahead of the September 16 General Election.

a2371.speaker: Meshack Kinyua, space engineer and Africa space policy veteran who oversees capacity-building at the African Space Agency
a2371.name: Meshack Kinyua
a2371.title: space engineer and Africa space policy veteran who oversees capacity-building at the African Space Agency
a2371.speech: "Space activities on the continent have been happening in a very fragmented fashion," said Kinyua. "The African Space Agency brings a coordination mechanism and economies of scale - it puts all members of the African Union at an equal level in terms of gathering data that they can access according to their needs."

a2371.speaker: Meshack Kinyua, space engineer and Africa space policy veteran who oversees capacity-building at the African Space Agency
a2371.name: Meshack Kinyua
a2371.title: space engineer and Africa space policy veteran who oversees capacity-building at the African Space Agency
a2371.speech: Said the African Space Agency is a step toward changing that, and that the agency also aims to scale up some successful initiatives happening across the continent, including early warnings systems for fishermen in western Africa and in the Congo river basin.

a2371.speaker: Meshack Kinyua, space engineer and Africa space policy veteran who oversees capacity-building at the African Space Agency
a2371.name: Meshack Kinyua
a2371.title: space engineer and Africa space policy veteran who oversees capacity-building at the African Space Agency
a2371.speech: "We need to ensure that African satellites can improve measurements and fill data gaps. These gaps will always be there, and we need to fill some of them ourselves, and engage with other agencies."

a2371.speaker: Meshack Kinyua, space engineer and Africa space policy veteran who oversees capacity-building at the African Space Agency
a2371.name: Meshack Kinyua
a2371.title: space engineer and Africa space policy veteran who oversees capacity-building at the African Space Agency
a2371.speech: "Getting financial resources is a challenge because there's so much we need to do, and our resources are limited. But we have to take baby steps before we start running."

a2371.speaker: Benjamin Koetz, head of the long term action section at the European Space Agency
a2371.name: Benjamin Koetz
a2371.title: head of the long term action section at the European Space Agency
a2371.speech: Said that in Europe, national space agencies share the cost of launching new Earth observation satellites, which can be as high as 800 million euros ($897 million). "Every country doesn't need to invest and build the same satellite," Koetz said.

a2371.speaker: Danielle Wood, associate professor who directs the Space Enabled Research Group at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
a2371.name: Danielle Wood
a2371.title: associate professor who directs the Space Enabled Research Group at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
a2371.speech: Said Africa's space pioneers - which include Nigeria, Egypt and South Africa - took a long time to set up their agencies and start operating because they started from scratch. "It shouldn't take that long now that many African countries have space experience, and hopefully the best outcome is that new countries can look at existing examples and coordinate to go faster," she said. "Other players like the US and Europe will have their own agenda, but the African Space Agency will be African-focused, so it should help every country in Africa."

a2371.speaker: Space In Africa (@spaceinafrica1), social media post
a2371.name: Space In Africa (@spaceinafrica1)
a2371.title: social media post
a2371.speech: "The inauguration of the African Space Agency holds special significance for us, having contributed to the journey through the baseline study for the establishment and operationalisation of the African Space Agency. This is the future of the African space programme."

a2416.speaker: Modeste Kerekou, Minister in charge of small and medium-sized enterprises of Benin (ministerial authority)
a2416.name: Modeste Kerekou
a2416.title: Minister in charge of small and medium-sized enterprises of Benin (ministerial authority)
a2416.speech: According to the ministerial authority, the objective of the fair is to make the know-how of Beninese artisans known to the whole world and to generate opportunities, and finally to instil a dynamic of healthy emulation among the players who drive the sector, for its influence.

a2416.speaker: Organising Committee of the National Handicrafts Fair of Benin (SNAB)
a2416.name: Organising Committee of the National Handicrafts Fair of Benin (SNAB)
a2416.speech: "Under the enlightened leadership of the Vice-President of the Republic, Mariam Chabi Talata Zime Yerima, patron of the event, this edition of the SNAB will take on a new and even stronger dimension in terms of visibility and prestige, with a view to facilitating market access for our artisans," and informed the public that for this year the guest country of honour is Morocco.

a2526.speaker: Sanlam Awards organisers
a2526.name: Sanlam Awards organisers
a2526.speech: “His reporting has informed the public, generated public debate and triggered regulatory scrutiny,” the organisers said of Ryk van Niekerk, the 2025 Sanlam Group Financial Journalist of the Year.

a2526.speaker: Sanlam Awards organisers
a2526.name: Sanlam Awards organisers
a2526.speech: the organisers said the award attracted 237 entries from 17 countries across the African continent this year, noting it is the highest entries ever in the competition's 50-year history.

a2698.speaker: White House Office of Management and Budget (internal planning document, the "Passback")
a2698.name: White House Office of Management and Budget (internal planning document
a2698.title: the "Passback")
a2698.speech: Proposed ending funding for UN peacekeeping missions, citing the failures of operations in Mali, Lebanon and the Democratic Republic of Congo: "The Passback provides no funding for CIPA, thereby ending contributions to international peacekeeping operations because of recent failures, such as MINUSMA, UNIFIL and MONUSCO, as well as because of the disproportionately high level of contribution."

a2698.speaker: White House Office of Management and Budget (internal planning document, the "Passback")
a2698.name: White House Office of Management and Budget (internal planning document
a2698.title: the "Passback")
a2698.speech: Proposes creating a fund entitled the American Opportunity Fund (A1OF) worth 2.1 billion dollars to finance a limited set of foreign aid and development priorities: "If the administration wishes to make contributions to the UN regular budget or to peacekeeping operations, we will seek to do so through the A1OF fund."

a2698.speaker: Reuters (news agency)
a2698.name: Reuters (news agency)
a2698.speech: Obtained access to the internal planning documents on which the report is based.

a2698.speaker: Anna Evstigneeva, Russia's Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN
a2698.name: Anna Evstigneeva
a2698.title: Russia's Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN
a2698.speech: Had stated that Russia considered "dubious" the participation of mercenaries from European private military companies in the UN Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO).

a2776.speaker: Scott Perry, U.S. Congressman (Republican, Pennsylvania)
a2776.name: Scott Perry
a2776.title: U.S. Congressman (Republican, Pennsylvania)
a2776.speech: Alleged during a congressional hearing that USAID had indirectly financed terrorist activities across the world, including in Nigeria ; accused USAID of inadvertently supporting extremist groups through its annual budget of $697 million ; cited concerns over cash flows to Islamic schools (madrasas), which he claimed had facilitated terrorist training.

a2776.speaker: Gen Christopher Musa, Nigeria's Chief of Defence Staff
a2776.name: Gen Christopher Musa
a2776.title: Nigeria's Chief of Defence Staff
a2776.speech: Had raised concerns about terrorist groups in the country receiving funding and training from international organisations.

a2776.speaker: Senator Ali Ndume
a2776.name: Senator Ali Ndume
a2776.speech: Raised a motion calling for an urgent investigation into the claims, after which Nigerian lawmakers on Wednesday issued summons.

a2805.speaker: Lucy Banda (Mai Lucy), maize-husk weaver and entrepreneur, Mitundu, Lilongwe
a2805.name: Lucy Banda (Mai Lucy)
a2805.title: maize-husk weaver and entrepreneur, Mitundu, Lilongwe
a2805.speech: "I started this business to support my family. It began as a small idea, but now it has grown into something I never imagined. Through this, I've managed to build a home for my family and send my children to school." ; "This is all I know. After my husband died, I had to take over. There was no other choice. I had to provide for my children, and weaving maize husks into carpets and baskets became my lifeline."

a2805.speaker: Lucy Banda (Mai Lucy), maize-husk weaver and entrepreneur, Mitundu, Lilongwe
a2805.name: Lucy Banda (Mai Lucy)
a2805.title: maize-husk weaver and entrepreneur, Mitundu, Lilongwe
a2805.speech: "People think maize husks are just waste, but for me, they are gold. It takes time to prepare them, and the weaving process is not easy. But when I see the final product, I know all the effort is worth it."

a2805.speaker: Lucy Banda (Mai Lucy), maize-husk weaver and entrepreneur, Mitundu, Lilongwe
a2805.name: Lucy Banda (Mai Lucy)
a2805.title: maize-husk weaver and entrepreneur, Mitundu, Lilongwe
a2805.speech: "There were times I worried about how I would afford my daughter's education, but this business has changed everything. Every sale I make is an investment in her future."

a2805.speaker: Lucy Banda (Mai Lucy), maize-husk weaver and entrepreneur, Mitundu, Lilongwe
a2805.name: Lucy Banda (Mai Lucy)
a2805.title: maize-husk weaver and entrepreneur, Mitundu, Lilongwe
a2805.speech: said if only she had more awareness and access to better markets, she could do much more: "I hope one day, our government and other organisations will see the potential in what we do and help us grow." ; said she is aware that there are organisations offering small business grants and low-interest loans to expand production capacity, but she does not know where she can go, and said she would like to partner with foreign trade organisations and embassies to connect her with more buyers abroad because she hears her products can fetch more money.

a2805.speaker: Ruth, daughter of Lucy Banda
a2805.name: Ruth
a2805.title: daughter of Lucy Banda
a2805.speech: "I help my mother collect the materials and put everything together. She is ageing now, and this job is not easy. I step in to help her weave because I want to see this business grow." ; "I want to see my mother's business flourish."

a2805.speaker: Ruth, daughter of Lucy Banda
a2805.name: Ruth
a2805.title: daughter of Lucy Banda
a2805.speech: "Now that the government has banned plastic bags, I hope they will promote alternatives like bags made from maize husks. These products are not only environment-friendly but also support local artisans like my mother."

a2805.speaker: Amy Diaz, United States Embassy Charge d'affaires in Malawi
a2805.name: Amy Diaz
a2805.title: United States Embassy Charge d'affaires in Malawi
a2805.speech: explains how she bought a rug from Mai Lucy Banda and has made it a conversation piece during official receptions and private gatherings at her residence, consistently earning praise; what made her happy was seeing how much more business such attention brought to Lucy. "Supporting entrepreneurs like her is just as vital as the large-scale development assistance we provide to Malawi." ; "People may struggle to grasp the scale of foreign aid figures, but they can easily understand the impact of one woman supporting her daughters, building a business and preserving Malawi's cultural heritage." ; said the growing recognition of Lucy's work is now encouraging more Malawians to purchase local artisan products, sparking hope for a broader revival of the country's rich artistic traditions.

a2805.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, economic commentator
a2805.name: Velli Nyirongo
a2805.title: economic commentator
a2805.speech: said all the women need is training and capacity building; that is, equipping artisans with skills in branding, marketing and e-commerce to strengthen their businesses ; "With the right support, Mai Lucy's journey can inspire many more Malawian entrepreneurs to turn local resources into globally admired products - generating forex for the country while empowering community members."

a2805.speaker: Sellina Mwenelupembe, chairperson of the Comesa Federation of Women in Business (COMFWB) Malawi Chapter
a2805.name: Sellina Mwenelupembe
a2805.title: chairperson of the Comesa Federation of Women in Business (COMFWB) Malawi Chapter
a2805.speech: has expressed the organisation's commitment to promoting women entrepreneurs, particularly those in the arts and crafts sector, which she says is a key source of foreign currency earnings: "There is potential in arts and crafts businesses run by women, who can contribute to Malawi's economic growth and job creation agenda. Arts and crafts is one of the best-performing sectors within COMFWB, in terms of foreign currency generation, especially among women entrepreneurs." ; said the organisation is currently seeking to connect with promising artisans such as Mai Lucy so that "we can provide training opportunities and source funding to help boost their businesses" ; emphasised that empowering women entrepreneurs remains key to sustainable economic development across the region, and said the global market for eco-friendly products is expanding, and in some countries items made from maize husks are highly valued and fetch good prices.

a2805.speaker: Francis Mwamadi, official of the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Institute (Smedi)
a2805.name: Francis Mwamadi
a2805.title: official of the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Institute (Smedi)
a2805.speech: said their interventions focus heavily on facilitating market access for MSMEs: "We facilitate participation in exhibitions organised by our partners, host our own fairs and promote MSME products through our website and social media platforms. Additionally, we have established fora in all regions where small businesses can share information on opportunities and connect with potential buyers. We actively facilitate interactions of buyers and sellers to help small businesses minimise the costs of prospecting for clients."

a3027.speaker: Minister of the Budget of Djibouti
a3027.name: Minister of the Budget of Djibouti
a3027.speech: Presented several texts. The purpose of the 1st draft Order is the allocation of a 3,000 sq m plot at Saline Ouest to the Ministry of Labour, placed at the disposal of the National Social Security Fund and intended for a maternity hospital; the 2nd grants the Ministry of Defence the definitive concession of an 89.5-hectare undeveloped plot in Balbala South for social housing; the 3rd allocates a 10,000 sq m plot in Nagad to the Higher Institute of Accounting and Business Administration for a private higher-education institute; the 4th transfers two built-up urban plots (one registered to National Education, the other the Islamic Institute) to the Embassy of Saudi Arabia in Djibouti; and the 5th allocates a 12.43-hectare plot in the Damerjog sector to the company CREC-DJIB SAS for the construction of a renewable energy park, which will support the national energy policy.

a3027.speaker: Minister of Urban Planning, Environment and Tourism of Djibouti
a3027.name: Minister of Urban Planning
a3027.title: Environment and Tourism of Djibouti
a3027.speech: Gave an account of his participation in the 25th Session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, held from 2 to 13 December 2019 in Madrid ; also gave a mission report on the 22nd Session of the Arab Ministerial Council for Tourism and on the signing of the memorandum of understanding between Saudi Arabia and Djibouti, held from 22 to 24 December 2019 in Saudi Arabia.

a3086.speaker: China-Africa Changsha Declaration on Upholding Solidarity and Cooperation of the Global South (FOCAC document)
a3086.name: China-Africa Changsha Declaration on Upholding Solidarity and Cooperation of the Global South (FOCAC document)
a3086.speech: Sent out a strong message for solidarity and cooperation of the Global South, in the firm belief that countries should uphold true multilateralism, safeguard the United Nations-centred international system, defend the World Trade Organisation-centred multilateral trading system and make economic globalisation more open, inclusive, mutually beneficial and balanced, so as to foster a better trade, investment and financing environment for the Global South.

a3086.speaker: China (announcement at the FOCAC ministerial coordinator's meeting)
a3086.name: China (announcement at the FOCAC ministerial coordinator's meeting)
a3086.speech: Announced that it will expand the zero-tariff treatment for 100 percent tariff lines to all 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with it, to help quality products from Africa access the Chinese market; for the least developed countries in Africa, China will roll out further measures on market access, inspection and quarantine, and customs clearance.

a3086.speaker: Chinese Ambassador to Zambia (author of the op-ed)
a3086.name: Chinese Ambassador to Zambia (author of the op-ed)
a3086.speech: Writes that in the face of frequent occurrence of unilateralism, protectionism and economic bullying by a certain country for selfish gains, the international community should give prioritised attention to the economic difficulties and development challenges faced by African countries, and that "development assistance to African countries should be increased, not unilaterally slashed, to provide continued support to help African countries improve people's livelihood, reduce poverty and boost economic and social development"; says he is confident that by advancing modernisation hand in hand, China and Zambia will further deepen the all-weather friendship and practical cooperation.

a3280.speaker: International AIDS Society (IAS)
a3280.name: International AIDS Society (IAS)
a3280.speech: Has reiterated the critical need for immediate action to restore access to all HIV services in Nigeria and other poor resource countries ; acknowledged the decision to waive the suspension of “life-saving humanitarian assistance”, including “core life-saving medicine” ; urgently called on policymakers and stakeholders to restore the funding lifeline to this pivotal programme. Lives depend on it, right now ; has said the action (Rubio's temporary waiver) is not enough ; insisted the emphasis should be on ensuring that, as a matter of urgency, PEPFAR implementers return to work to ensure that access to critical HIV services is not further interrupted and that communities most in need are able to get the care and treatment they need.

a3280.speaker: International AIDS Society (IAS)
a3280.name: International AIDS Society (IAS)
a3280.speech: Had last Friday warned that the immediate freezing of funding to the U.S. President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), including a stop-work order for existing grants and contracts, portends a looming crisis for millions, worldwide.

a3280.speaker: Beatriz Grinsztejn, IAS President
a3280.name: Beatriz Grinsztejn
a3280.title: IAS President
a3280.speech: Alerted in a statement that the immediate freezing places millions of lives in jeopardy: “On Day 1 of taking office as US President, Donald Trump signed an executive order that banned any new government spending on foreign aid projects. This was followed by an unexpected ‘stop-work order’ issued on 24 January, which means that funding to PEPFAR, even for existing grants and contracts, is frozen.” ; “This is a matter of life or death. PEPFAR provides lifesaving antiretrovirals for more than 20 million people – and stopping its funding essentially stops their HIV treatment. If that happens, people are going to die and HIV will resurge.” ; “It makes no sense to suddenly stop this incredible catalyst of our global progress towards ending HIV as a threat to public health and individual well-being.”

a3280.speaker: Beatriz Grinsztejn, IAS President
a3280.name: Beatriz Grinsztejn
a3280.title: IAS President
a3280.speech: Maintained: “Since its bipartisan creation, PEPFAR has always been synonymous with saving lives and this waiver restores – in some part – that legacy. However, PEPFAR’s continued and uninterrupted support of all HIV treatment and prevention services must be fully restored.” ; “PEPFAR has been and should continue to be an active contributor to changing the trajectory of the HIV epidemic. It is our hope that this waiver remains in place and will be expanded to all HIV services.”

a3280.speaker: PEPFAR (report)
a3280.name: PEPFAR (report)
a3280.speech: Reports that PEPFAR’s lifesaving work is enabled through the U.S. government’s unwavering commitment to the program and the American people’s compassion and generosity, as PEPFAR ensures every U.S. taxpayer dollar is optimally focused on impact.

a3280.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a3280.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a3280.speech: Warned of adverse consequences of the immediate suspension of funding for HIV programmes in Nigeria and other low- and middle-income countries under PEPFAR ; alerted that the move would upset HIV programmes and have a direct impact on millions of lives that depend on the regular supply of safe and effective antiretroviral treatment (ART) ; urged the Trump administration to create more exemptions to ensure the delivery of lifesaving HIV treatment and care in the affected countries.

a3280.speaker: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director General of WHO
a3280.name: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a3280.title: Director General of WHO
a3280.speech: Expressed worry over the development and said programmes that will be affected by the funding cut provide critical HIV therapy to over 30 million people worldwide. In a statement, Tedros cautioned that a funding freeze could raise the risk of illness and death for those living with HIV and hinder efforts to prevent the spread of the virus within communities. He said that if the situation continues, it could lead to more new infections and deaths, undoing years of progress, and could return the world to the 1980s and 1990s, a time when millions died from HIV each year, including many in the United States.

a3280.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a3280.name: Marco Rubio
a3280.title: US Secretary of State
a3280.speech: On 28 January, issued a temporary waiver of aspects of this freeze.

a3457.speaker: European Union Delegation to Libya (message posted on its official page)
a3457.name: European Union Delegation to Libya (message posted on its official page)
a3457.speech: Praised the resilience of the Libyan people and reiterated its continued support for the country's peace and nation-building efforts, reaffirming its commitment to stand by the Libyan people and emphasizing its "continued support on the path toward peace, unity, and prosperity for all citizens" ; stated: "Today, Libya celebrates its Liberation Day, which is a moment to honour the resilience, courage, and aspirations of the Libyan people", paying tribute to those who have worked for more than a decade to stabilize the country; reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Libyan-led efforts toward a lasting resolution of the conflict, reiterated its backing for initiatives promoting political dialogue, national reconciliation, and the restoration of legitimate state institutions under the auspices of the United Nations, and emphasised that Libya's stability remains a regional priority and a key factor for peace and prosperity across the Mediterranean basin.

a3540.speaker: Bafou Ba, President of the Senegalese Red Cross
a3540.name: Bafou Ba
a3540.title: President of the Senegalese Red Cross
a3540.speech: Emphasized the urgent need for enhanced protection of the humanitarian organization’s globally recognized emblem and called for intensified advocacy efforts with national authorities to highlight the critical economic, security, and political-diplomatic implications associated with safeguarding the emblem; stressed the importance of raising public awareness regarding the existing legislation governing its proper use and expanding avenues for collaboration within the humanitarian sector.

a3540.speaker: Bafou Ba, President of the Senegalese Red Cross
a3540.name: Bafou Ba
a3540.title: President of the Senegalese Red Cross
