a3540.speech: Expressed her concern over the persistent and recurring instances of misuse, imitation, and unauthorized appropriation of the Red Cross emblem, despite ongoing public awareness campaigns, and urged increased vigilance and more rigorous enforcement of the relevant laws.

a3540.speaker: Cheikh Talibou Djimbera, Director of the National Service for Education and Health and Social Information at the Ministry of Health and Social Action
a3540.name: Cheikh Talibou Djimbera
a3540.title: Director of the National Service for Education and Health and Social Information at the Ministry of Health and Social Action
a3540.speech: Reaffirmed his ministry’s commitment to supporting the Senegalese Red Cross and pledged a strengthened partnership, broader dissemination of awareness messages, and strict enforcement of the legal frameworks designed to protect the emblem.

a3540.speaker: Fally Sadio, Head of Communications for the Senegalese Red Cross
a3540.name: Fally Sadio
a3540.title: Head of Communications for the Senegalese Red Cross
a3540.speech: Said the emblem transcends being a mere logo, its historical significance being profound, having lent its name to the earliest relief societies and subsequently to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) as early as 1875, and that the emblem serves the dual purpose of protecting relief personnel and clearly identifying members of the Movement ; lamented, “Unfortunately, we are currently witnessing a misuse of the emblem’s intended purpose, including imitation, usurpation, or perfidy. These are serious acts that risk diminishing its protective value and undermining the effectiveness of humanitarian assistance” ; emphasized that any unauthorized use of the Red Cross, Red Crescent, and their respective names constitutes an illegal act punishable under international humanitarian law, the Geneva Conventions and their additional protocols, and Senegalese Law No. 2013-711 of August 5, 2013.

a3560.speaker: Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (CDEDI) and Malawi Palestine Solidarity Movement (MPSM)
a3560.name: Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (CDEDI) and Malawi Palestine Solidarity Movement (MPSM)
a3560.speech: Are demanding explanations from President Lazarus Chakwera as to why the Malawi government voted against a Gaza ceasefire, and are also demanding explanation from Chakwera on the new map of Tanzania that includes Lake Malawi; the groupings believe that Tanzania’s new map including Lake Malawi is clear indication that the lake has been taken away to Tanzania.

a3560.speaker: Sylvester Namiwa, CDEDI Executive Director, and Asubin Phiri, MPSM National Coordinator (news conference, 9 January 2024)
a3560.name: Sylvester Namiwa
a3560.title: CDEDI Executive Director, and Asubin Phiri, MPSM National Coordinator (news conference, 9 January 2024)
a3560.speech: Want Chakwera to come out from the cocoon to address the Gaza war, Lake Malawi and fuel crises.

a3560.speaker: Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (CDEDI) (statement)
a3560.name: Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (CDEDI) (statement)
a3560.speech: “As the September 16, 2025 General Election draws closer, the Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (CDEDI) feels duty-bound to draw the public’s attention to some significant matters that it fears, if not handled properly now, will have far-reaching implications, but authorities are deliberately avoiding to talk about such important matters”; said the acute shortage of fuel, food, fertilizer, forex and essential medical supplies in public health facilities is a clear manifestation of the current government’s cluelessness and lack of direction.

a3560.speaker: Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (CDEDI) (statement)
a3560.name: Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (CDEDI) (statement)
a3560.speech: Said it is appalling that the Malawi Congress Party-led government is burying its head in the sand instead of taking affirmative action on issues such as the Lake Malawi boundaries with neighbouring Tanzania; said CDEDI is deeply shocked with the laissez-faire attitude with which it is being handled in Malawi, and is challenging the Malawi Government Spokesperson, Hon Moses Kumkuyu, to come out clearly on whether the silence means the Malawi government has accepted the new boundaries as depicted on the map he received as a gift from Tanzania; said that if so, President Dr. Lazarus Chakwera’s administration should accept that they have failed to uphold the Republican Constitution and the noble thing to do is to resign immediately.

a3560.speaker: CDEDI and the Malawi Palestine Solidarity Movement (MPSM) (joint statement)
a3560.name: CDEDI and the Malawi Palestine Solidarity Movement (MPSM) (joint statement)
a3560.speech: Said there is an apparent contradiction between Malawi’s commitment to the Rome Statute and its vote at the recent United Nations General Assembly against the resolution supporting the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza; warned that unless government rescinds its position, which is an apparent support to the Gaza genocide, the future of the much-touted Government-to-Government fuel agreement with any country in the Middle East will remain a far-fetched dream; said the vote was perceived as supporting Israel’s continued military actions and has created a negative perception among other UN member-States, with potential consequences for Malawi’s international reputation, diplomatic relations, economy (“reduced foreign aid or investment from countries that oppose Israel’s actions”), humanitarian standing and legal exposure.

a3560.speaker: CDEDI and the Malawi Palestine Solidarity Movement (MPSM) (joint statement – recommendations and demands)
a3560.name: CDEDI and the Malawi Palestine Solidarity Movement (MPSM) (joint statement – recommendations and demands)
a3560.speech: Recommended that Malawi publicly reaffirm its commitment to the Rome Statute and the ICC’s mission, align its UNGA voting with commitment to justice and human rights by supporting resolutions calling for cessation of hostilities and protection of civilians in Gaza, engage in diplomatic efforts, and educate the public and government officials; demanded that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs explain to Malawians, within seven days, at what forum the ‘no’ vote was discussed and the justification for that decision, and that the Ministry of Justice inform the nation, also within seven days, whether it advised the President before the voting took place and whether it believes Malawi’s stand is right.

a3606.speaker: GIZ and Cordaid (press statement)
a3606.name: GIZ and Cordaid (press statement)
a3606.speech: In a press statement, the development partners said 18 boreholes will be available for clean water access, with 7 boreholes being newly drilled and 11 currently nonfunctional boreholes being rehabilitated. In addition, three rehabilitated boreholes will be upgraded with solar-powered technology. ; “Working directly with smallholder farmers and cooperatives in Nzara and Yambio and Aweil West and Aweil Centre in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, the project aims to support farmers in increasing their harvest and providing a more varied and healthier diet to their families by boosting the productivity of their farms,” the statement said. ; The drilling of the new boreholes and the rehabilitation and upgrading of non-functional boreholes will be done by Greta Ruaha Drilling Company Limited in villages within the counties of Nzara and Yambio, it added.

a3606.speaker: GIZ assessment conducted in 2023 (report)
a3606.name: GIZ assessment conducted in 2023 (report)
a3606.speech: An assessment conducted by GIZ in 2023 found that many communities in the counties Yambio and Nzara depend on run-off surface water from streams and rivers, and often lack access to clean water, sanitation and hygiene services.

a3606.speaker: GIZ
a3606.name: GIZ
a3606.speech: The organization underscored that access to clean and safe water and sanitation is a human right and reflected in goal 6 of the Sustainable Development Goals adopted by the United Nations in 2015.

a3677.speaker: Taa Wongbe, Nimba County Representative and founder of the Khana Group
a3677.name: Taa Wongbe
a3677.title: Nimba County Representative and founder of the Khana Group
a3677.speech: Is calling on Liberians to view the Afrobarometer Survey Report from a non-political lens because its methodology is rigorous, objective, and data-driven, and the findings, irrespective of political context, offer invaluable insights for improving governance and performance ; “I can state unequivocally that Afrobarometer’s methodology is rigorous, objective, and data-driven. Its findings, irrespective of political context, offer invaluable insights for improving governance and performance. It is unfortunate that, at times, politics can overshadow the critical role of data in informing policy and progress. I hope we can approach the data without the lens of politics, allowing it to serve as a tool for honest reflection and as a pathway to move our country forward,” Mr. Wongbe passionately said.

a3677.speaker: Taa Wongbe, Nimba County Representative and founder of the Khana Group
a3677.name: Taa Wongbe
a3677.title: Nimba County Representative and founder of the Khana Group
a3677.speech: On the Khana Group’s Afrobarometer contract: “This recognition was a testament to our firm’s solid track record and expertise in conducting high-quality, independent research, like we had done for USAID, Gallup, the World Bank, and other 100 other clients and partners globally. Our team completed the survey with the utmost professionalism and integrity, and the resulting data was widely appreciated by key partners including the World Bank, USAID, the UN, and the Government of Liberia. However, during this period, Eugene Fahngon, who was serving in the CDC administration as Deputy Information Minister, turned the report political, and raised concerns about my potential for impartiality due being an opposition and my role as Senior Political Advisor to Mr. Alexander B. Cummings. He communicated these concerns directly to the Ghana Center for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana), which manages the Afrobarometer study. Subsequently, CDD-Ghana, with regret, decided to terminate our contract prematurely, though it was intended to be an annual engagement.”

a3677.speaker: Ambulah Mamey, public policy analyst and Unity Party supporter
a3677.name: Ambulah Mamey
a3677.title: public policy analyst and Unity Party supporter
a3677.speech: Noted that, in as much as the Rescue Mission is succeeding in impacting the lives of Liberians, the Boakai-led administration needs to step up its national recovery gamesmanship; said the Afrobarometer data shows that the Rescue Mission was successful, however the recovery efforts are struggling, even though more people are still hopeful things will get better ; “In 2018, 30% of Liberians said Liberia was going in the right direction. In 2022, the percentage dropped to 25%. Today, 50% of Liberians believe Liberia is heading in the right direction. This means more people believe Liberia was RESCUED and being placed in the right direction. RESCUE Mission Successful!!! But rescuing people – while is the first important effort – it is not sufficient when they are still painfully struggling for recovery. The data also shows 50% of Liberians are not happy about JNB-JKK recovery efforts. No jobs! The good news however is that over 60% of Liberians (including those complaining about the struggling recovery process) believe things will get better. JNB-JKK won in 2023 with 50.6% so this 60% who believe things will get better means over 9% of Liberians who did not believe in 2023 that JNB-JKK couldn’t do better, now believe that JNB-JKK would do better. Every administration prays to have more people believing in them and giving them a chance to deliver even if things are difficult. That is exactly what the data shows JNB-JKK have currently. They can look at the 60% and decide to relax or they can look at the fact that 50% of the people, eventhough hopeful, are not happy. For us, we are very pleased that more Liberians believe today that their country was RESCUED from the wrong direction. We will now push JNB-JKK to deliver the recovery promises, or we replace them with a better recovery team that can take our country forward, not backward,” Mr. Mamey said in a social media post in reaction to the Afrobarometer Survey report.

a3677.speaker: Mohammed K. Jalloh, CDC stalwart
a3677.name: Mohammed K. Jalloh
a3677.title: CDC stalwart
a3677.speech: Said the head of the Center for Democratic Governance (CDG), Attorney Oscar Bloh, is a Unity Party sympathizer working in the interest of the Boakai administration and therefore skewed the Afrobarometer data in favor of the government ; “The Unity Party representative in Oscar Bloh conducted what can only be described as one of the most biased surveys in Liberia’s history. Despite the significant economic hardships faced by both Liberians and foreign residents, this individual falsely claims that 50% of Liberians believe that Boakai’s ineffective government is heading in the right direction. He was seen in the Unity Party’s election war room alongside Amara Konneh, managing the UP election data. It should be noted that this so-called report lacks independence and credibility. Unity Party, you are fooling yourselves, not the masses of our people. Our citizens deserve better than this baseless survey,” Mr. Jalloh vented.

a3677.speaker: Blama Kiawu, CDC supporter
a3677.name: Blama Kiawu
a3677.title: CDC supporter
a3677.speech: Said the Afrobarometer is a complete mess: “I think they should find place to hide themselves with their fake reports on the living conditions of the Liberian people,” he said.

a3677.speaker: Afrobarometer (May 30, 2025 survey report)
a3677.name: Afrobarometer (May 30
a3677.title: 2025 survey report)
a3677.speech: The survey result showed how Liberians are equally divided in their assessment of the country’s direction and the economy.

a3677.speaker: Supporters of the ruling Unity Party
a3677.name: Supporters of the ruling Unity Party
a3677.speech: Continue to hail the report’s finding as indicative of the marked improvements in the country’s governance and economic outlooks under the Boakai-led administration.

a3677.speaker: Staunch supporters of the ousted CDC
a3677.name: Staunch supporters of the ousted CDC
a3677.speech: Call it a propagandistic piece of work sponsored by the ruling Unity Party, terming the report as skewed to favor the Unity Party.

a3753.speaker: US Department of State
a3753.name: US Department of State
a3753.speech: Says that from 8 July nearly all non-immigrant and non-diplomatic visas issued to Nigerian citizens will now be single-entry and valid for only three months; says this is part of a global reciprocity realignment ; says visa policies remain “subject to ongoing review” and may change depending on evolving diplomatic, security, and immigration benchmarks.

a3753.speaker: US government (statement)
a3753.name: US government (statement)
a3753.speech: Said it was working closely with Nigerian authorities to ensure the country meets key international standards, including issuing secure travel documents, managing visa overstays, and sharing security or criminal data for public safety purposes ; ordered that the social media accounts of all foreigners applying for visas, including from Nigeria, would be vetted for “any indications of hostility toward the citizens, culture, government, institutions, or founding principles of the United States”.

a3753.speaker: 2024 Open Doors report on international education exchanges, published by the US Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs
a3753.name: 2024 Open Doors report on international education exchanges
a3753.title: published by the US Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs
a3753.speech: According to the report, Nigeria was the seventh largest source of international students to the US, and the highest in Africa, showing a 13.5% increase from 2023.

a3753.speaker: Bashir Ahmad, aide to former Nigerian President Muhammadu Buhari
a3753.name: Bashir Ahmad
a3753.title: aide to former Nigerian President Muhammadu Buhari
a3753.speech: Said he believed the US was not reciprocating but showing its displeasure with Nigeria, posting on X that President Bola Tinubu's recent visit to Brazil for the Brics gathering was behind the move ; “This is not solely about reciprocity. Rather, it appears to reflect growing US discomfort with Nigeria's increasing global realignment, particularly the warm reception we are receiving from the Brics.”

a3897.speaker: Benedict Okey Oramah, outgoing President of Afreximbank
a3897.name: Benedict Okey Oramah
a3897.title: outgoing President of Afreximbank
a3897.speech: In his farewell address, looked back on the philosophy that guided his decade at the head of the institution: making intra-African trade and investment the engine of the continent's development. “Our conviction was that the only viable path to Africa's economic emancipation lay in reversing the colonial strategy of 'divide and rule' and in building a development model founded on our own strengths,” he declared ; recalled the major progress achieved thanks to this vision: the launch of innovative financial mechanisms, the implementation of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), now operational in 20 countries, and the creation of the AfCFTA Adjustment Fund, endowed with one billion dollars to support states in implementing African free trade.

a3897.speaker: George Elombi, President-designate of Afreximbank
a3897.name: George Elombi
a3897.title: President-designate of Afreximbank
a3897.speech: Paid a strong tribute to his predecessor, describing him as “a rare leader, combining vision and the capacity to execute” ; “Under his leadership, Afreximbank laid the foundations of robust intra-African trade and sustainable industrial development. He turned the political wishes of entire generations into concrete achievements.”

a3987.speaker: Dr Da-Costa Aboagye, Chief Executive Officer of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3987.name: Dr Da-Costa Aboagye
a3987.title: Chief Executive Officer of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a3987.speech: Told the Daily Graphic in Accra that the initiative, on the theme “Addressing Non-Communicable Diseases and Chronic Diseases in Ghana”, was the preventive aspect of health care ; said it would offer comprehensive annual health screening for blood pressure, blood sugar, and Body Mass Index (BMI) testing, along with counselling and referrals as needed ; “The initiative provides an opportunity for all Ghanaians aged 18 and above, irrespective of NHIS enrolment, to access health care at any credentialed provider nationwide” ; said at the launch that it was a demonstration of the government and the NHIA's commitments to enhancing health care access and reducing disease incidence ; “Our Free Annual Health Checkup programme is designed to prevent severe health conditions, reduce healthcare costs and improve quality of life” ; “The initiative aims to increase life expectancy, reduce healthcare costs and accelerate the achievement of universal health coverage and Sustainable Development Goal Three” ; emphasised the importance of disease prevention and using the initiative to increase NHIA membership, saying it was also in line with the global shift towards preventive health care, stressing the benefits of early detection and intervention ; said a nationwide orientation would be carried out to encourage Ghanaians to take advantage of the Free Annual Health Checkup to safeguard their health and contribute to a healthier and more productive nation.

a3987.speaker: Dr Da-Costa Aboagye, Chief Executive Officer of the NHIA (on partners and stakeholders)
a3987.name: Dr Da-Costa Aboagye
a3987.title: Chief Executive Officer of the NHIA (on partners and stakeholders)
a3987.speech: Acknowledged the collaborative efforts of various stakeholders, including the Ministry of Health, the Ghana Health Service, Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG), private health facilities, teaching hospitals, the Society of Private Medical and Dental Health Practitioners, and community leaders ; expressed gratitude to development partners such as the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) for their support and dedication to improving public health in the country ; “The NHIA will work with its partners to ensure they are well equipped to deliver this high-quality screening. This programme is not just about testing, but also about educating our population on healthy lifestyles and preventive measures.”

a3987.speaker: Joseph Codjoe, Minister of Public Enterprises (delivering the keynote address on behalf of Samira Bawumia, wife of the Vice-President)
a3987.name: Joseph Codjoe
a3987.title: Minister of Public Enterprises (delivering the keynote address on behalf of Samira Bawumia, wife of the Vice-President)
a3987.speech: Highlighted the significance of the initiative as one of two biggest policies, along with the Free Senior High School policy the government introduced to improve the lives of Ghanaians ; “Ghanaians are encouraged to utilise the Free Annual Health Checkup for early detection of health issues, enabling better life planning.”

a4091.speaker: World Bank
a4091.name: World Bank
a4091.speech: According to the World Bank, full implementation of the AfCFTA could boost intra-African Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) by 68 percent and external investment by 122 percent.

a4273.speaker: Lesetja Kganyago, SARB Governor
a4273.name: Lesetja Kganyago
a4273.title: SARB Governor
a4273.speech: Said the committee wanted to observe the full effects of previous rate reductions on the economy before making further adjustments. "The transmission of past monetary policy actions is ongoing, and we need to ensure that these measures effectively support growth while keeping inflation expectations anchored," he said.

a4273.speaker: Analysts
a4273.name: Analysts
a4273.speech: Say the SARB's cautious approach signals that further rate cuts, if any, will likely be gradual.

a4438.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a4438.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a4438.title: Vice President of Liberia
a4438.speech: Emphasized that these new facilities symbolize a fresh chapter in Liberia's environmental journey: "This laboratory reflects the importance of the EPA's mandate. It provides our staff with a clean, functional, and dignified workspace, and allows Liberia to take its place among nations that are seriously addressing the global climate and environmental crisis." ; "For many years, Liberia's EPA lacked the scientific infrastructure it needed to do its job effectively. Despite receiving advanced equipment from international partners like the International Atomic Energy Agency, the EPA simply did not have the facilities to deploy or maintain these tools." ; "It is a foundation for evidence-based regulation. This is how we will monitor water quality, test for air pollution, track coastal erosion, analyze climate data, and make informed policy decisions to protect public health and the environment."

a4438.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a4438.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a4438.title: Vice President of Liberia
a4438.speech: Highlighted that while the new headquarters represents a major advancement, it is not the final goal, disclosing that plans are already underway to construct a permanent, climate-resilient EPA headquarters, a flagship building powered entirely by renewable energy and showcasing green building technology, with a projected timeline for completion of three to five years.

a4438.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a4438.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a4438.title: Vice President of Liberia
a4438.speech: Emphasized the lab's role in enhancing Liberia's compliance with international climate commitments, particularly under the Paris Agreement: "Environmental protection is not just about trees and rivers. It's about people, protecting farmers from drought, coastal communities from erosion, and our children from toxic air and water." ; He extended thanks to Liberia's development partners and all stakeholders supporting the country on this important journey.

a4438.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo, EPA Executive Director
a4438.name: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo
a4438.title: EPA Executive Director
a4438.speech: Said the facility represents a strategic investment that aligns with Liberia's growing emphasis on environmental governance ; He revealed that the EPA Board has already approved the purchase of both the current building and the adjacent property, which will house the new laboratory.

a4438.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo, EPA Executive Director
a4438.name: Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo
a4438.title: EPA Executive Director
a4438.speech: Highlighted Liberia's progress in preparing for participation in the carbon market, supported by international partners such as the Coalition of Rainforest Nations, UNDP, and Novasphere: "Our goal is to raise significant revenue from the carbon market to support the ARREST Agenda and our updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0)." ; "This policy defines ownership of carbon credits, outlines equitable benefit-sharing mechanisms, and establishes a clear institutional framework, all essential under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement," adding, "Liberia is positioning itself to responsibly harness the carbon market and ensure that our natural resources generate real benefits for our people."

a4623.speaker: Joakim Reiter, Chief External & Corporate Affairs Officer for Vodafone Group (Vodafone Foundation spokesperson)
a4623.name: Joakim Reiter
a4623.title: Chief External & Corporate Affairs Officer for Vodafone Group (Vodafone Foundation spokesperson)
a4623.speech: Emphasised the importance of addressing the lack of affordable transport for pregnant women in rural areas: “Seventy percent of the world's maternal deaths occur in sub-Saharan Africa, and we believe this initiative can significantly reduce those numbers in Malawi.”

a4623.speaker: Joakim Reiter, Chief External & Corporate Affairs Officer for Vodafone Group
a4623.name: Joakim Reiter
a4623.title: Chief External & Corporate Affairs Officer for Vodafone Group
a4623.speech: “We are thrilled to see such strong support from USAID and other donors, and we are confident that the Government of Malawi will commit to sustaining this lifesaving service.”

a4715.speaker: Adedeji Stanley Dhikrullahi Olajide (Odidiomo), Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Digital, Information Communication Technology and Cybersecurity
a4715.name: Adedeji Stanley Dhikrullahi Olajide (Odidiomo)
a4715.title: Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Digital, Information Communication Technology and Cybersecurity
a4715.speech: Urged stakeholders across the country to adopt a holistic approach in tackling terrorism in Nigeria, stressing the need for a more indigenous response to the lingering security crisis and noting that local intelligence and homegrown solutions would play a critical role in countering terrorism: "Terrorism is a global challenge that has plagued even the most powerful nations in the world. However, reliance on foreign support alone cannot solve this problem. We must look inward and establish mechanisms that are tailored to our unique security realities." ; Emphasized that while international collaboration remains crucial, the Nigerian government must develop a self-sustaining strategy to prevent external influences from dictating the country's security architecture, and called for increased investment in intelligence gathering, community-based security initiatives and enhanced synergy between security agencies and local stakeholders: "Our security framework must be robust enough to neutralize threats at their roots. The involvement of local communities, traditional rulers and grassroots intelligence operatives cannot be overemphasized."

a4715.speaker: Adedeji Stanley Dhikrullahi Olajide (Odidiomo), Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Digital, Information Communication Technology and Cybersecurity
a4715.name: Adedeji Stanley Dhikrullahi Olajide (Odidiomo)
a4715.title: Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Digital, Information Communication Technology and Cybersecurity
a4715.speech: Stressed the importance of transparency and accountability in foreign aid and NGO operations within Nigeria, stating that the ongoing investigation by the Ad-hoc Committee was crucial in ensuring that external interventions align with national security interests: "We must ensure that every organization operating within our borders adhere strictly to national laws and does not, under any guise, compromise our national security. The allegations made against USAID by a U.S. Congressman must be thoroughly investigated to ascertain the veracity of these claims and take appropriate actions where necessary."

a4715.speaker: Adedeji Stanley Dhikrullahi Olajide (Odidiomo), Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Digital, Information Communication Technology and Cybersecurity
a4715.name: Adedeji Stanley Dhikrullahi Olajide (Odidiomo)
a4715.title: Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Digital, Information Communication Technology and Cybersecurity
a4715.speech: Reiterated his committee's commitment to strengthening cybersecurity policies and enhancing Nigeria's digital infrastructure to curb the spread of extremist ideologies online and across the digital space.

a4715.speaker: A United States Congressman
a4715.name: A United States Congressman
a4715.speech: Made allegations against the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) over alleged terrorism funding, which the House of Representatives Ad-hoc Committee was inaugurated to investigate.

a4721.speaker: Silver Ojakol, Chief of Staff, African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat
a4721.name: Silver Ojakol
a4721.title: Chief of Staff, African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat
a4721.speech: Has challenged business and political leaders to be intentional in utilising the Continent's vast natural resources for its development ; noted that for years, Africa's resources had powered global development at the detriment of the continent and its people, and asked business and political leaders to change the narrative through AfCFTA ; "There is an urgent need for us [Africa] to use our vast natural resources and the demographic advantage for industrialisation, improved infrastructure and energy solutions that will enhance and reduce production cost."

a4721.speaker: Gabby Otchere-Darko, Founder/Executive Chairman, African Prosperity Network
a4721.name: Gabby Otchere-Darko
a4721.title: Founder/Executive Chairman, African Prosperity Network
a4721.speech: Called for "a big push within the first 10 years of the agreement coming into force [2021 and 2031] to achieve Africa's economic integration." ; said the summit was aimed at changing the narrative and focusing on the prosperity of the continent.

a4721.speaker: Eugene Owusu, Board Member, African Prosperity Network
a4721.name: Eugene Owusu
a4721.title: Board Member, African Prosperity Network
a4721.speech: "We are too rich to be poor! So, we must define our narrative - one that inspires hope and self-confidence and one that speaks to our human dignity." ; encouraged Africa to transform its development misfortunes by scaling up production, adding value to what was produced, and addressing obstacles and deepening intra-African trade.

a4744.speaker: Pius Kennedy, Ugandan LGBTQ+ rights activist and employee of the Africa Queer Network
a4744.name: Pius Kennedy
a4744.title: Ugandan LGBTQ+ rights activist and employee of the Africa Queer Network
a4744.speech: “Some donors are now going to pull out resources because they were also receiving from the similar funding baskets to sub grant to us” ; according to Kennedy, the funding cuts mean reversing years of gains in the country ; said USAID had been the biggest funder of HIV programs, with around 20 million people receiving drugs and testing services through associated organisations.

a4744.speaker: Pius Kennedy, Ugandan LGBTQ+ rights activist and employee of the Africa Queer Network
a4744.name: Pius Kennedy
a4744.title: Ugandan LGBTQ+ rights activist and employee of the Africa Queer Network
a4744.speech: Amid uncertainty on the future of US funding, underscored the immediate impact on at-risk individuals in the world’s poorest communities, decrying that survivors of gender-based violence have nowhere to turn for medical or psychological support.

a4744.speaker: Pius Kennedy, Ugandan LGBTQ+ rights activist and employee of the Africa Queer Network
a4744.name: Pius Kennedy
a4744.title: Ugandan LGBTQ+ rights activist and employee of the Africa Queer Network
a4744.speech: Expressed concern about the impact of tougher conditions on asylum seekers and fears that LGBTQ+ people under threat in Uganda will no longer be able to claim asylum in the US ; “I’m looking at this not as an issue that affected Uganda or that affected East Africa, it’s an issue that has affected the global citizenship.”

a5118.speaker: Abderrazzak Zebdani, Deputy Managing Director of the Bank of Africa (BOA) Group
a5118.name: Abderrazzak Zebdani
a5118.title: Deputy Managing Director of the Bank of Africa (BOA) Group
a5118.speech: Presented the 2022 financial results of the Group's six listed UEMOA subsidiaries at an online press conference on Wednesday, April 12, 2023, showing a total balance sheet of 4,540 billion CFA francs and a net profit of 92.9 billion CFA francs ; "With the exception of BOA-Ghana, the results of all our subsidiaries are beyond our targets," he said with satisfaction.

a5118.speaker: Abderrazzak Zebdani, Deputy Managing Director of the Bank of Africa (BOA) Group
a5118.name: Abderrazzak Zebdani
a5118.title: Deputy Managing Director of the Bank of Africa (BOA) Group
a5118.speech: Stressed that these results are the outcome of the group's strategic vision, broken down into three strategic pillars: digital transformation; balance-sheet transformation, which has translated into colossal investments in networks and staff training and a reorientation of the portfolio towards individuals and SMEs, with more than half of outstanding loans now coming from individuals; and trade finance. He indicated that for SMEs the Group has developed a package of specific services made up of advisory support, technical assistance and training in cash and stock management and in mastering import/export processes ; "We cannot be a Group with a significant and varied presence and not be a major player in international trade."

a5118.speaker: Abderrazzak Zebdani, Deputy Managing Director of the Bank of Africa (BOA) Group
a5118.name: Abderrazzak Zebdani
a5118.title: Deputy Managing Director of the Bank of Africa (BOA) Group
a5118.speech: Responding to journalists on the question of the BCEAO's call to commercial banks for prudence in the distribution of dividends, said that beyond this directive from the regulator, the sharing of dividends at BOA obeys three fundamental principles: ensuring its growth from its own funds independently of shareholders, complying with the various regulatory ratios, and maintaining a harmonious level of dividend distribution.

a5118.speaker: BCEAO (Central Bank of West African States)
a5118.name: BCEAO (Central Bank of West African States)
a5118.speech: Invited commercial banks to exercise prudence in the distribution of dividends.

a5169.speaker: H.E. James Knight, Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin (opinion piece for World AIDS Day)
a5169.name: H.E. James Knight
a5169.title: Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin (opinion piece for World AIDS Day)
a5169.speech: “On the occasion of World AIDS Day 2009, we gather as a global community to draw attention to and celebrate great progress against AIDS in the world. Over the past 25 years, the international health community has made important advances in the fight against the HIV/AIDS pandemic – advances that deserve to be saluted on this World AIDS Day.”

a5169.speaker: H.E. James Knight, Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin / US Embassy in Benin
a5169.name: H.E. James Knight
a5169.title: Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin / US Embassy in Benin
a5169.speech: “For the Embassy of the United States in Benin, it is particularly exciting to say that the American people, through USAID, support the social marketing of male and female condoms as part of HIV/AIDS prevention.” Likewise, USAID supports behaviour-change communication activities among the most at-risk groups, notably young people and truck drivers; supports HIV prevention among young people through the strategy of delaying first sexual intercourse; each month thousands of copies of the USAID-financed magazine Amour et Vie are distributed in school and university settings; in the northern regions a local NGO offers STI management, counselling and voluntary testing; in Zou, Collines and Alibori USAID supports prevention of mother-to-child transmission; during 2008 USAID provided testing kits to the National AIDS Control Programme; and USAID is strengthening the management and coordination capacities of the National Committee for the Fight against HIV/AIDS.

a5169.speaker: H.E. James Knight, Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin
a5169.name: H.E. James Knight
a5169.title: Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin
a5169.speech: “Together, we have also provided care to more than 10 million people affected by HIV/AIDS, including more than 4 million orphans and vulnerable children, and we have supported programmes to prevent mother-to-child transmission of the virus that have allowed nearly 240,000 newborns to come into the world free of HIV infection.”

a5169.speaker: H.E. James Knight, Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin
a5169.name: H.E. James Knight
a5169.title: Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin
a5169.speech: “The United States remains firm in its commitment to fight AIDS, but the United States cannot defeat AIDS in isolation... That is why we must continue to work hand in hand with these countries and with our international partners to overcome the many obstacles that still stand in our path.” ; “The United States, in collaboration with our multilateral partners, civil society and non-governmental organisations, must support countries that seek to strengthen their AIDS response programmes over the long term. We must continue to support the efforts designed by the countries themselves so that universal access to treatment becomes a reality for all their citizens, and to examine openly the fundamental rights questions that aggravate the HIV/AIDS pandemic.”

a5228.speaker: Healthcare staff in the Zambezi Region
a5228.name: Healthcare staff in the Zambezi Region
a5228.speech: expressed gratitude for the progress achieved through support from USAID, as these initiatives have significantly enhanced service delivery and health outcomes in the region.

a5438.speaker: Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA)
a5438.name: Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA)
a5438.speech: Taking stock of its accomplishments and setbacks in 2024, described the past year as one of resilience and progress, characterised by a mix of triumphs and challenges.

a5438.speaker: Chikosola Chuula, IBA Board chairperson
a5438.name: Chikosola Chuula
a5438.title: IBA Board chairperson
a5438.speech: Noted during the end-of-year press briefing that despite the challenges, significant strides were made in enhancing Zambia’s broadcasting landscape, with several key milestones achieved: “Ladies and gentlemen, I am now pleased to share the key highlights of the authority’s performance in 2024. The Guidelines for the Enforcement and Handling of Compliance Breaches, launched in 2023, have improved the regulation of the broadcasting industry.”

a5438.speaker: Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA)
a5438.name: Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA)
a5438.speech: Reported improvements in broadcast sound, picture quality and more professional production standards, attributing the development to the government’s announcement of a three-year tax waiver on broadcasting equipment in 2023.

a5438.speaker: Chikosola Chuula, IBA Board chairperson
a5438.name: Chikosola Chuula
a5438.title: IBA Board chairperson
a5438.speech: “The government’s waiver on customs duty for broadcasting equipment has already shown signs of creating a more viable, competitive, and technologically advanced broadcasting sector, positioning Zambia’s broadcasting industry for sustained growth and success in the coming years.”

a5438.speaker: Chikosola Chuula, IBA Board chairperson
a5438.name: Chikosola Chuula
a5438.title: IBA Board chairperson
a5438.speech: On the ongoing process to repeal and replace the IBA Act, said the authority felt that frequent amendments to the 2002 Act have led to confusion and legal ambiguities, which the new Act seeks to resolve for better clarity and effective regulation; the authority is convinced that the move would address legal ambiguities and provide for a licensing framework that is responsive to technological advancements.

a5438.speaker: Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA) (end-of-year report)
a5438.name: Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA) (end-of-year report)
a5438.speech: Reported that as of December 2024 Zambia had 190 radio stations and 66 television stations, a total of 256; that three new licences were granted following successful appeals to the Minister of Information and Media; that Radio France International (RFI)’s operations in Zambia were regularised and Voice of America (VOA) was granted permission to extend its coverage to Kitwe; that capacity-building training was conducted for 104 broadcasting stations in eight provinces engaging approximately 200 participants; that 89 cases of non-compliance with licensing conditions were recorded, eight broadcasting licences suspended and three stations’ licences cancelled or surrendered; and that a “Cooling-off Window” allowing stations to switch off equipment between midnight and 06:00 hours in response to load-shedding has been extended to the end of February 2025.

a5496.speaker: Council of East and Central Africa Football Associations (CECAFA) (statement published on the association's website)
a5496.name: Council of East and Central Africa Football Associations (CECAFA) (statement published on the association's website)
a5496.speech: Has announced that 12 teams will participate in the regional Kagame Cup 2025, scheduled to take place in Dar es Salaam from September 2nd to 15th.

a5496.speaker: Auka Gecheo, CECAFA Executive Director
a5496.name: Auka Gecheo
a5496.title: CECAFA Executive Director
a5496.speech: Expressed enthusiasm about the tournament, stating: "We are happy to announce that the tournament will take place from September 2-15 in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania" ; clarified that the competition will feature 12 teams, with the host country providing two teams, as well as an additional guest team from another zone ; "We expect this to be a more competitive tournament, as most teams will use it as preparations for the 2025/2026 CAF competitions."

a5728.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a5728.name: Sam Matekane
a5728.title: Prime Minister of Lesotho
a5728.speech: “High youth unemployment has been worsened by changing global trade dynamics, US foreign aid cuts, and the imposition of reciprocal tariffs. Young people need help.”

a5728.speaker: Official government notice dated July 7 (Lesotho)
a5728.name: Official government notice dated July 7 (Lesotho)
a5728.speech: According to it, the law — which gives the government additional powers including bypassing standard procedures — will be in force for two years.

a5728.speaker: Lesotho's finance minister
a5728.name: Lesotho's finance minister
a5728.speech: Revealed in February that 38 percent of the country’s youth were unemployed.

a5728.speaker: Government of Lesotho
a5728.name: Government of Lesotho
a5728.speech: Has warned it could lose up to 40,000 jobs if AGOA is not renewed at the end of September.

a5728.speaker: Kananelo Boloetse (@YourKayBol), social media post
a5728.name: Kananelo Boloetse (@YourKayBol)
a5728.title: social media post
a5728.speech: Posted Lesotho's unemployment rate from 2010 to 2023 (27.9% in 2010 falling to 24.9% in 2019 and rising to 28.5% in 2023), citing the World Bank as the source.

a5740.speaker: Analysis published in the Journal of the International Aids Society (February)
a5740.name: Analysis published in the Journal of the International Aids Society (February)
a5740.speech: Shows that the 90-day halt in funding from the President's Emergency Plan for Aids Relief (Pepfar), because of President Donald Trump ordering a freeze on US foreign aid, would lead to 100 000 extra Aids-related deaths in the next year.

a5740.speaker: Jirair Ratevosian, former head of staff at Pepfar and associate research scientist at Yale University
a5740.name: Jirair Ratevosian
a5740.title: former head of staff at Pepfar and associate research scientist at Yale University
a5740.speech: "Pepfar will change as a result of the [US] foreign aid review," told Bhekisisa in a podcast in February ; said it is hard to predict how Pepfar will come out at the other end, especially with Congress's reauthorisation decision due on March 25: "But one thing is for sure: Pepfar is not going to look the same."

a5740.speaker: Mitchell Warren, executive director of the New York-based advocacy organisation Avac
a5740.name: Mitchell Warren
a5740.title: executive director of the New York-based advocacy organisation Avac
a5740.speech: Explains, "At least at this point, it appears that some aspects of Pepfar and the funding for Global Fund, will continue."

a5740.speaker: Global Fund investment case for its eighth replenishment cycle (published February)
a5740.name: Global Fund investment case for its eighth replenishment cycle (published February)
a5740.speech: Figures show that getting the total deaths from HIV, TB and malaria down to under 1-million by 2029 would need a commitment of $18-billion from donors over the next three years; further shows that every $1 donated in this cycle would yield $19 worth of health benefits over the next three years.

a5740.speaker: Global Fund 2024 results report
a5740.name: Global Fund 2024 results report
a5740.speech: Shows that without their donors' money, deaths from each of these diseases would likely have close to doubled in the last 20 years.

a5740.speaker: The Global Fund for HIV, Tuberculosis and Malaria
a5740.name: The Global Fund for HIV
a5740.title: Tuberculosis and Malaria
a5740.speech: Says they will stand by their commitment to help pay for 2-million people to get at least one shot of the twice-a-year anti-HIV jab lenacapavir - with or without the US's help.

a5740.speaker: Study results (on lenacapavir)
a5740.name: Study results (on lenacapavir)
a5740.speech: Showed that the medicine was 100% effective in preventing young cisgender women from contracting HIV.

a5740.speaker: Peter Sands, the Global Fund's executive director
a5740.name: Peter Sands
a5740.title: the Global Fund's executive director
a5740.speech: Said in an interview with Bhekisisa earlier this month: "We cannot afford to miss such a game-changing opportunity."

a6000.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, European Union Ambassador to Malawi
a6000.name: Rune Skinnebach
a6000.title: European Union Ambassador to Malawi
a6000.speech: Has expressed concerns over the worsening economic difficulties Malawians are facing; said in an exclusive interview with Malawi News that Malawi is at a crucial point - just like the rest of the world - that requires tough decisions to stop the country's economy from sliding further ; "Life is getting harder, and the country is facing serious challenges." ; said the foreign exchange crisis is one of Malawi's biggest economic problems today, adding that climate-related disasters have added to the weight of the problem; called for strict financial discipline, better revenue collection and urgent debt restructuring to stabilise the economy ; "With elections approaching, the big question is how Malawi will handle these tough times. Many are waiting for the upcoming national budget to see what direction the government will take."

a6000.speaker: Marvin Banda, economist
a6000.name: Marvin Banda
a6000.title: economist
a6000.speech: Said as global economic conditions become more difficult and with foreign governments increasingly looking inward, developing countries like Malawi that are dependent on aid are in for the toughest of times ; "As nationalism grows worldwide, international financial support is shrinking. Skinnebach is absolutely right that we face really tough times." ; said Malawi's economy is being artificially supported such that while some indicators may seem stable now, it is only a matter of time before the situation worsens for the people.

a6000.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, economist
a6000.name: Velli Nyirongo
a6000.title: economist
a6000.speech: Feared that Malawi could fall deeper into economic trouble ; "The government must make tough decisions, such as whether to devalue the kwacha or introduce policies that encourage local production and reduce reliance on imports." ; said for ordinary Malawians the forex crisis is more than just numbers, as it affects whether they can afford food, keep their jobs, or access medicine, and that without urgent action life will only get harder.

a6000.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Minister of Finance
a6000.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a6000.title: Minister of Finance
a6000.speech: Admitted the tight spot in which Malawi finds itself, but said the government is putting up measures to fix the economic situation and improve the quality of life of people, and that some of the challenges are caused by speculative economic theories that are causing panic ; "When I came in as Minister of Finance, I analysed and diagnosed Malawi's economic challenges as forex, fuel, food and fertiliser. Today we are still grappling with the same challenges because as a country we are not producing enough to offset the trade balance. We are importing more than what we are exporting. We need to focus on production using the mega farms, mining also. Then our case will be different. That's why even our yet-to-be-presented budget will be productivity-based." ; said the government is focusing on productivity "so that we produce more and more for domestic and external markets so that we can generate more forex", and is working on both macro and microeconomic elements to stabilise the economy.

a6207.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad (communiqué)
a6207.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a6207.title: Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad (communiqué)
a6207.speech: Published a communiqué sharply criticising the European delegation’s management of the 1.3 million euros of humanitarian aid for flood victims, stressing that this aid had been made available “without it having requested it.”

a6207.speaker: Nigerien authorities
a6207.name: Nigerien authorities
a6207.speech: Said the EU Ambassador had “unilaterally” allocated the grant to several NGOs, notably the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and Cooperazione Internazionale (COOPI); denounced a “disregard for the principles of transparency and good collaboration” and particularly criticised the “arbitrary” distribution of the funds by region.

a6207.speaker: State of Niger
a6207.name: State of Niger
a6207.speech: Announced the launch of an audit into the management of the funds mentioned and a formal request to the European Union that it also carry out an audit in order to “know the real use and destination of the sums allocated to the NGOs concerned.”

a6207.speaker: European Union
a6207.name: European Union
a6207.speech: Announced on Saturday 23 November the recall of its ambassador to Niger for consultations in Brussels ; In its response, expressed “its profound disagreement with the allegations” and recalled that humanitarian aid is provided “in a neutral, impartial and independent manner” through United Nations agencies and international organisations, maintaining its willingness to support the Nigerien population while denouncing any “instrumentalisation of humanitarian aid for political ends.”

a6211.speaker: Lazare Sèhouéto, Beninese MP, president of the Force clé party, member of the Union fait la Nation and former minister of agriculture and trade
a6211.name: Lazare Sèhouéto
a6211.title: Beninese MP, president of the Force clé party, member of the Union fait la Nation and former minister of agriculture and trade
a6211.speech: Sounded the alarm about the threat hanging over the 2012-2013 cotton season: “The hour is grave and if we are not careful, the Beninese economy risks taking a blow.” ; Said he is worried about the very short time available to obtain inputs in order to launch this year’s cotton campaign, and drew public attention to the politicisation surrounding the call for tenders for the importation of inputs, saying the cotton sector is going through a bad patch and risks experiencing a blank year.

a6211.speaker: Lazare Sèhouéto, Beninese MP, president of the Force clé party, member of the Union fait la Nation and former minister of agriculture and trade
a6211.name: Lazare Sèhouéto
a6211.title: Beninese MP, president of the Force clé party, member of the Union fait la Nation and former minister of agriculture and trade
a6211.speech: Contrary to the government’s forecasts of reaching production of 500,000 tonnes by 2015, considers that the way the sector is being managed will not allow that result to be reached, and puts current production at 200,000 tonnes at most, a record which in his view reflects the underperformance of the ‘refoundation’ regime; said that in his day, when he was minister of agriculture, he was able to bank 428,000 tonnes ; Acknowledges that the quality of Beninese cotton has greatly improved in recent years, so that Benin today occupies first place in the sector, a position that risks slipping away because of the delay in the tender process.

a6211.speaker: Lazare Sèhouéto, Beninese MP, president of the Force clé party, member of the Union fait la Nation and former minister of agriculture and trade
a6211.name: Lazare Sèhouéto
a6211.title: Beninese MP, president of the Force clé party, member of the Union fait la Nation and former minister of agriculture and trade
a6211.speech: Speaks of approximate management by the government and deplores the attitude of Minister Sabaï Katé, who halted the call-for-applications process: “Ghana has not been able to recover, to this day, from the blank cotton year it experienced in 1984,” he pointed out ; Concluded that it is a scandal that risks occurring if the head of state does not take the measure of the danger threatening the sector, “since there is no point in sidelining, for partisan political considerations, the sector’s thinkers, at a time when the country’s most important resource is on the way to disappearing.”

a6457.speaker: Amadou Keita, Mali's Minister of Mines
a6457.name: Amadou Keita
a6457.title: Mali's Minister of Mines
a6457.speech: Assured on Friday on social media that Mali will integrate its mineral wealth into the “overall quest” for its stability, declaring at an ordinary session of the Economic, Social, Environmental and Cultural Council (CESEC) that “the discovery of new (geological) indices must not be perceived as a simple matter of mining investment. Today, it is a geopolitical and geostrategic issue that Mali has an obligation to integrate into its overall quest for stability” ; “So-called strategic or critical minerals are reshuffling the cards of international relations and of the balance of power”, adding that Mali, “rich in rare earths and other strategic substances, is today in a position to develop these indices, by determining the reserves and positioning itself as an actor on the world market” ; welcomed the diversification of mining shown by the opening on 15 December of a lithium mine at Goulamina and by oil exploration, while stressing that this diversification policy was encountering “enormous challenges” linked to investment.

a6457.speaker: Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI/ITIE)
a6457.name: Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI/ITIE)
a6457.speech: According to the EITI, mining represents about 10% of Malian GDP and 22% of Mali's public revenues, with gold representing 80% of exports.

a6565.speaker: Jean-Pierre Rousseau, Project Director, Winrock International, USAID
a6565.name: Jean-Pierre Rousseau
a6565.title: Project Director, Winrock International, USAID
a6565.speech: Stated that over two million smallholder Nigerian farmers have accessed about $40.8 million in credit facilities through USAID's 'Innovative Market-led Extension Delivery' project in three years ; said the project has exposed 2.021 million smallholder farmers to new information, technologies and services in Benue, Cross River, Delta, Ebonyi, Kaduna, Kebbi and Niger states, with greater access to improved agricultural technologies and financial access working with micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) on alternative models of extension delivery.

a6565.speaker: Jean-Pierre Rousseau, Project Director, Winrock International, USAID
a6565.name: Jean-Pierre Rousseau
a6565.title: Project Director, Winrock International, USAID
a6565.speech: Said the summit becomes necessary to share the project's impact with other key stakeholders within and outside Nigeria to catalyse adoption and sustainability across the 36 states and the FCT.

a6565.speaker: Ben Odoemena, Chief of Party, USAID Feed the Future Agricultural Extension and Advisory Services Activity in Nigeria
a6565.name: Ben Odoemena
a6565.title: Chief of Party, USAID Feed the Future Agricultural Extension and Advisory Services Activity in Nigeria
a6565.speech: Said the project has identified 39 most impactful practices (MIPs) as key extension innovation messages or business solutions that MSMEs need to reach smallholder farmers to enhance their capacity ; said about 70% of the improved agricultural practices are climate smart to help farmers adapt or build resilience to climate change.

a6664.speaker: Dr Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.name: Dr Akinwumi Adesina
a6664.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.speech: Warned that higher U.S. tariffs could trigger significant economic disruptions across Africa, affecting numerous nations and accelerating a strategic shift in global partnerships, and revealed in an exclusive interview with CNN's Christiane Amanpour that 47 of Africa's 54 countries will be impacted directly by the new U.S. trade policies, with potential declines in export revenues and foreign exchange reserves: "When those currencies weaken, two things will happen: first, you will find that most of these countries are import-dependent. So, you're going to find that high inflation becomes a problem. And secondly, you find that the cost of actually servicing a lot of their debt, which is foreign currency debt, but in local currencies, is going to get worse."

a6664.speaker: Dr Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.name: Dr Akinwumi Adesina
a6664.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.speech: Emphasised that Africa cannot afford a trade confrontation with the United States, noting that the continent accounts for only 1.2 percent (approximately $34 billion) of America's global trade, with a trade surplus of just $7.2 billion, and proposed a pragmatic three-point strategy: engage the U.S. through flexible and constructive trade negotiations, diversify export markets to reduce dependency on any single partner, and accelerate African Continental Free Trade Area implementation to unlock the potential $3.4 trillion market; stressed the need to expand Africa's domestic market and boost domestic savings, and to take advantage of increasing external interest in natural resources such as cobalt and lithium to negotiate a better trade and investment deal.

a6664.speaker: Dr Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.name: Dr Akinwumi Adesina
a6664.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.speech: Dismissed any notion of binary alignment with China: "U.S is a key ally of Africa - and so is China. Africa is building bridges, not isolating itself." ; stressed that Africa seeks balanced, transparent and mutually beneficial partnerships with all major global players, including the U.S., China, the European Union and the Gulf states: "I think at the end of the day, we want to make sure that whatever deals that are being done with Africa are transparent, fair, equitable, and led by Africa and in Africa's interests."

a6664.speaker: Dr Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.name: Dr Akinwumi Adesina
a6664.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.speech: Firmly rejected the long-standing paradigm of foreign aid dependency: "The era of aid as we've known it is completely gone," calling instead for bold investments in domestic resource mobilization, infrastructure and value-added industrialization, and saying aid must be turned into concessional financing to allow multilateral financial institutions like the African Development Bank to do more for the continent by mobilizing more private capital to develop and derisk projects.

a6664.speaker: Dr Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.name: Dr Akinwumi Adesina
a6664.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.speech: Pointed to a resilient and transformative growth narrative, noting that ten of the world's twenty fastest-growing economies are in Africa; highlighted flagship initiatives under the Bank's "High 5" agenda that have impacted more than 565 million people, and cited the great potential of Mission 300, the joint World Bank and African Development Bank initiative to connect 300 million people in Africa to electricity by 2030: "Because without electricity, what can you do? You can't industrialize, you can't add value, you can't be competitive in the dark."

a6664.speaker: Dr Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.name: Dr Akinwumi Adesina
a6664.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6664.speech: Highlighted the achievements of the Africa Investment Forum, launched in 2018 by the Bank and eight other partners, saying it has since mobilized more than $225 billion in investment interest to the continent, and said that despite its challenges Africa is the largest greenfield investment destination in the world and remains "the investor's dream": "We got hydropower. We have a massive youth population that can become the labor force of the world. Sixty-five percent of the arable land left in the world to feed almost 9.5 billion people by 2050 is in Africa, so what Africa does with it will determine the future of food in the world."

a6858.speaker: Observatory of Economic Complexity
a6858.name: Observatory of Economic Complexity
a6858.speech: According to the Observatory of Economic Complexity, Rwanda exported $885 million worth of gold in 2023, making gold the country’s top export product.

a6858.speaker: The United Nations and various NGOs
a6858.name: The United Nations and various NGOs
a6858.speech: Have repeatedly accused Rwanda of acting as a laundering hub for Congolese gold, masking its origins and creating the illusion of a legitimate export trade.

a6858.speaker: United Kingdom (government)
a6858.name: United Kingdom (government)
a6858.speech: Announced last week that it will impose sanctions on Rwanda.

a6976.speaker: ECOWAS heads of state (extraordinary summit, 24 February, Abuja)
a6976.name: ECOWAS heads of state (extraordinary summit
a6976.title: 24 February, Abuja)
a6976.speech: Announced during their meeting the reopening of Niger's land borders and airspace, and, for humanitarian reasons, also authorised financial transactions between the community's countries and Niger and unfroze the Nigerien state's assets, lifting with immediate effect a large part of the sanctions against Niger.

a6976.speaker: Gado Guidami, Mayor of Malanville
a6976.name: Gado Guidami
a6976.title: Mayor of Malanville
a6976.speech: Confirmed that the border on Niger's side is still closed: "Niger has not yet opened it, unlike Benin, which, since 5 September and well before this ECOWAS decision, had already freed everything up" ; "On Niger's side, it is still hermetically closed. Despite the ECOWAS decision, and up to the present hour, it is still not open to allow the populations to cross it, to go from one country to the other" ; said that this does not facilitate movement.

a6976.speaker: Gado Guidami, Mayor of Malanville
a6976.name: Gado Guidami
a6976.title: Mayor of Malanville
a6976.speech: Confided that informally the populations try to get by thanks to river transport on the Niger and its tributaries: "From the landing stages built on either side, taking pirogues, boats or makeshift rafts, and then taking the risk of drowning at any moment, they find the means to come and go with their goods, whether on Niger's side or on Benin's."

a6976.speaker: Ambroise Fonteclounon, Beninese trader
a6976.name: Ambroise Fonteclounon
a6976.title: Beninese trader
a6976.speech: "The closing of the borders with Niger, since the 26 July putsch, has never prevented me from continuing to sell my pineapples in the markets of Niamey. It is only the costs that have increased, not to mention the spoilage to be deplored with river transport and the journey, which also takes many days" ; "When the lifting of the sanctions was announced, I thought I had found relief."

a6976.speaker: Moussa Azizou, Nigerien trader
a6976.name: Moussa Azizou
a6976.title: Nigerien trader
a6976.speech: "Unfortunately, I can no longer stock up on cereals and tubers to go and resell them in Niamey," he regrets, after an important part of his merchandise ended up at the bottom of the Niger river and he had to send his truck back into Niger via Lome.

a7267.speaker: Government of Tanzania
a7267.name: Government of Tanzania
a7267.speech: Says the measure recognising additional sources of revenue for the AIDS Trust Fund is aimed at strengthening the national response to HIV/AIDS and accelerating the provision of universal health insurance ; says the changes to gaming taxes are designed to provide additional resources for the fight against HIV/AIDS and to strengthen efforts to roll out universal health coverage nationwide.

a7267.speaker: Finance Bill 2025 / Finance Act 2025 (Bill tabled in Parliament)
a7267.name: Finance Bill 2025 / Finance Act 2025 (Bill tabled in Parliament)
a7267.speech: Outlines key fiscal measures intended to support priority sectors while diversifying the national revenue base: it seeks to amend Section 18 of the AIDS Commission Act, Cap. 379, to recognise additional sources of revenue for the AIDS Trust Fund (excise duties on alcoholic beverages, a new HIV Response Levy on minerals and charges on train and airline tickets); proposes amendments to the Universal Health Insurance Act, Cap. 161; proposes increasing the airport service charge by 1,000/- per air passenger, with 70 per cent of the additional revenue channeled to the AIDS Trust Fund and 30 per cent to the Universal Health Insurance Fund; proposes raising the tax on winnings from sports betting from 10 to 15 per cent and on land-based casino winnings from 12 to 15 per cent; proposes a reduction in excise duty on locally produced energy drinks from 561/- to 134.2/- per litre; proposes excise duty exemption on undenatured ethyl alcohol used in the production of non-alcoholic goods; and sets a fixed rate of 1.5 per cent of business licence fees as part of the Fair Competition Commission's revenue, obliging EWURA, LATRA, TCRA and TCAA to remit 1 per cent of their gross revenue to a special FCC account at the Bank of Tanzania.

a7271.speaker: Donald Porusingazi, political analyst
a7271.name: Donald Porusingazi
a7271.title: political analyst
a7271.speech: Explained to APA on Friday that "Closing American companies would cause mass layoffs, disrupt supply chains and create panic among investors." ; "For the United States, the impact would also be significant, particularly in the sectors that depend on South Africa's strategic minerals, such as platinum, manganese and chromium, which are essential for industrial and technological applications. A sudden halt in exports would force the United States to look for other suppliers, probably at higher cost."

a7271.speaker: Donald Porusingazi, political analyst
a7271.name: Donald Porusingazi
a7271.title: political analyst
a7271.speech: Warned that such an action would not go unnoticed in Washington: "The United States has always reacted severely to economic restrictions imposed by foreign governments, and South Africa could face sanctions, the removal of its trade privileges or even diplomatic isolation."

a7271.speaker: Donald Porusingazi, political analyst
a7271.name: Donald Porusingazi
a7271.title: political analyst
a7271.speech: Stressed that such a measure, although unprecedented, could mark a bold assertion of African autonomy in global trade and economic policy: "Historically, African countries have often been the victims of Western economic decisions. A retaliatory stance against American financial policies would challenge traditional power structures, prompting other nations to rethink their economic dependencies."

a7271.speaker: Donald Porusingazi, political analyst
a7271.name: Donald Porusingazi
a7271.title: political analyst
a7271.speech: "South Africa has neither the economic scale of China nor that of Russia; it does not have the leverage needed to counter the potential fallout from a negative American reaction."

a7271.speaker: Donald Porusingazi, political analyst
a7271.name: Donald Porusingazi
a7271.title: political analyst
a7271.speech: "Does this scenario highlight Africa's dependence on Western economies? Absolutely; and it underlines the need for African countries to diversify their trade relations and strengthen regional economic resilience."

a7335.speaker: Ethiopian Public Health Institute (EPHI) report / Ethiopia Service Provision Assessment (ESPA), done in partnership with the Ministry of Health and financed by the federal government and USAID
a7335.name: Ethiopian Public Health Institute (EPHI) report / Ethiopia Service Provision Assessment (ESPA)
a7335.title: done in partnership with the Ministry of Health and financed by the federal government and USAID
a7335.speech: A significant drop in providing HIV tests has been recorded in health care during pregnancy follow-ups across the country; the report indicates that although a third quarter of health facilities nationwide offer antenatal care (ANC) services, only 36pc are capable of diagnosing HIV compared to the previous research in 2014. ; According to the recent report, the prevalence of HIV cases is estimated to be over half a million people while 7,194 new infections were detected in 2023.

a7335.speaker: Fikeresilasie Getachew, national survey coordinator of the report
a7335.name: Fikeresilasie Getachew
a7335.title: national survey coordinator of the report
a7335.speech: Indicated that private health institutions massively contributed to the declined rate observed where only 42pc test for HIV. "Most of them claim not to have testing kits or capacity," he said.

a7335.speaker: Solomon Nigussie, deputy director general, Ethiopian Pharmaceuticals Supply Service (EPSS)
a7335.name: Solomon Nigussie
a7335.title: deputy director general, Ethiopian Pharmaceuticals Supply Service (EPSS)
a7335.speech: Asserted that they have six months of stock; over 60pc of the 7.8 million HIV testing kits procured last year have been distributed nationwide and they are expecting 12.5 million kits in the fiscal year from Global Fund; indicated the type was changed a year ago to enhance the efficiency to 99pc while the algorithm was changed to testing three times. "We revised the amount of kits given to health facilities based on the number of positive results," he said. "But maternity care is an exception."

a7335.speaker: Ministry of Health (Ethiopia)
a7335.name: Ministry of Health (Ethiopia)
a7335.speech: In 2017, 12,000 maternal deaths were recorded, according to the Ministry of Health.

a7335.speaker: Ayenew Melese, Admin, Betsegah Mothers' and Children's Hospital
a7335.name: Ayenew Melese
a7335.title: Admin, Betsegah Mothers' and Children's Hospital
a7335.speech: Estimates a monthly follow-up for 3,000 expectant mothers and 150-200 deliveries; observed fluctuations in the testing kit delivery this year after the hospital was included under Kirkos District from Bole District nearly two months ago, and said the new administration has relaxed the delivery schedule with no kits inflow for a month. "We're sending them to test for HIV in other health facilities for now," said Ayenew.

a7335.speaker: Officials at the Addis Abeba Health Bureau
a7335.name: Officials at the Addis Abeba Health Bureau
a7335.speech: Disclosed directing procedures for testing individuals with a high-risk potential.

a7335.speaker: Seife Demissie, director of pharmaceutical supply & service directorate, Addis Abeba Health Bureau
a7335.name: Seife Demissie
a7335.title: director of pharmaceutical supply & service directorate, Addis Abeba Health Bureau
a7335.speech: "Our testing procedures have changed into testing potentially risked individuals only," he said – the risky individuals being people who were engaged in unprotected sexual intercourse, in contact with blood and sharp things, and sex workers.

a7335.speaker: Kedir Seid (MD), strategic affairs executive officer at the Ministry of Health
a7335.name: Kedir Seid (MD)
a7335.title: strategic affairs executive officer at the Ministry of Health
a7335.speech: Said the assessment duration is extended due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the national security situation and the process of securing a budget from a donor. "This requires further understanding of the reasons," Kedir told Fortune.

a7335.speaker: Naod Firdu (MD), public health expert at Addis Abeba University
a7335.name: Naod Firdu (MD)
a7335.title: public health expert at Addis Abeba University
a7335.speech: Argues that the kits are far from expensive with most funded from non-governmental organisations, and that the awareness level has plummeted, so the public should be encouraged to check for HIV rather than limit the kit. "The positive yield will increase after testing the general public," he told Fortune.

a7339.speaker: Khalid, 32, resident at Kashkak in Zenda Jan district
a7339.name: Khalid
a7339.title: 32, resident at Kashkak in Zenda Jan district
a7339.speech: "Many people have come from far-flung districts to get people out from the rubble." ; "Everyone is busy searching for bodies everywhere, we don't know if there are others as well under the debris."

a7339.speaker: Afghanistan's disaster agency
a7339.name: Afghanistan's disaster agency
a7339.speech: Said Sunday that 2,053 people had died; local and national officials gave conflicting counts of the number of dead and injured.

a7339.speaker: World Health Organisation
a7339.name: World Health Organisation
a7339.speech: Said more than 11,000 people had been affected from 1,655 families.

a7339.speaker: Save the Children
a7339.name: Save the Children
a7339.speech: Called the quake "a crisis on top of a crisis."

a7339.speaker: Arshad Malik, Save the Children country director
a7339.name: Arshad Malik
a7339.title: Save the Children country director
a7339.speech: "The scale of the damage is horrific. The numbers affected by this tragedy are truly disturbing."

a7477.speaker: United Nations Environmental Programme (UNEP) report on the environmental impacts of the Israeli genocide in Gaza
a7477.name: United Nations Environmental Programme (UNEP) report on the environmental impacts of the Israeli genocide in Gaza
a7477.speech: According to the report, the enclave has become an environmental ticking time bomb: aside from the complete degeneration of human civilisation and health systems, underground water, vegetation and water bodies have been severely contaminated, and air pollution resulting from bombing, infrastructural collapse and rubble is heartrending; the ecosystem necessary for healthy living has been destroyed.

a7483.speaker: Press release of the 64th UN meeting
a7483.name: Press release of the 64th UN meeting
a7483.speech: “The Assembly also adopted a draft resolution on cooperation between the United Nations and the Council of Europe (document A/79/L.75) by 105 votes to nine (Belarus, Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, Eritrea, Mali, Nicaragua, Niger, Russian Federation, Sudan, United States) with 33 abstentions.”

a7483.speaker: US delegate to the United Nations
a7483.name: US delegate to the United Nations
a7483.speech: Stated after the vote that the resolution was not conducive to peace.
